title.raw: 卷一上 高帝紀上 Volume 1: Annals of Emperor Gaozu 1

sentences.zh: 高祖，沛豐邑中陽里人也，姓劉氏。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was a person of Zhongyang Village, Fengyi Town, Pei County, and his surname was Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was born in Zhongyang Village in the town of Fengyi, Pei County. His surname was Liu.

sentences.zh: 母媼嘗息大澤之陂，夢與神遇。

translations.literal: His mother the old woman once rested by the dike of the great marsh, and dreamed of encountering a god.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while resting by the dike of a vast marsh, his mother dreamed that she encountered a divine being.

sentences.zh: 是時雷電晦冥，父太公往視，則見交龍於上。

translations.literal: At this time thunder and lightning were dark and obscure, father Taigong went to look, then saw two dragons entwining above.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment, thunder crashed and darkness fell. His father, Taigong, went to investigate and saw two dragons entwined in the sky above.

sentences.zh: 已而有娠，遂產高祖。

translations.literal: Soon after she became pregnant, and then gave birth to the Supreme Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, she became pregnant and gave birth to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖為人，隆準而龍顏，美須髯，左股有七十二黑子。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor as a person had a high nose and dragon face, beautiful beard and whiskers, and on his left thigh there were seventy-two black moles.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had a prominent nose, a face like a dragon, beautiful whiskers and beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 寬仁愛人，意豁如也。

translations.literal: Broadly benevolent and loving people, his intentions were magnanimous and open.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous, benevolent, and loved people. His mind was open and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 常有大度，不事家人生產作業。

translations.literal: Constantly having great breadth of mind, he did not engage in the family's production and work.
translations.idiomatic: He always showed great magnanimity and never concerned himself with the family's farming and business.

sentences.zh: 及壯，試吏，為泗上亭長，廷中吏無所不狎侮。

translations.literal: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official, became the pavilion chief of Sishang, and among the officials in the court there was none he did not treat with familiarity and insult.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official and became pavilion chief of Sishang. Among the officials at court there was none he did not treat with familiar disrespect.

sentences.zh: 好酒及色。

translations.literal: He favored wine and sex.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and women.

sentences.zh: 常從王媼、武負貰酒，時飲醉臥，武負、王媼見其上常有怪。

translations.literal: He constantly obtained wine on credit from Wang Po and Wu Fu, sometimes drank until drunk and lay down; Wu Fu and Wang Po saw that above him there was constantly something strange.
translations.idiomatic: He often bought wine on credit from Wang Po and Wu Fu. Sometimes he drank until he lay down drunk. Wu Fu and Wang Po saw that strange things constantly appeared above him.

sentences.zh: 高祖每酤留飲，酒讎數倍。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor each time he bought wine would stay and drink, the wine price several times.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozu bought wine, he stayed to drink, and the bill was several times higher.

sentences.zh: 及見怪，歲竟，此兩家常折券棄責。

translations.literal: When they saw the strange signs, at year's end these two households would always tear up the IOUs and abandon the debts.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw the strange omens, at the end of the year the two households would always tear up the wine tabs and forgive what he owed.

sentences.zh: 高祖常繇咸陽，縱觀秦皇帝，喟然大息，曰：「嗟乎，大丈夫當如此矣！」

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor often performed corvée service at Xianyang and was allowed to observe the Qin emperor; he sighed deeply and said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu often passed through Xianyang and gazed upon the Qin emperor. He would sigh deeply and say: "Ah, this is how a true man should live!"

sentences.zh: 單父人呂公善沛令，辟仇，從之客，因家焉。

translations.literal: Shanfu person Lü Gong was friendly with the Pei magistrate, avoided enmity by becoming his guest, and thus settled his household there.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong from Shanfu was on good terms with the magistrate of Pei. To avoid his enemies, he became the magistrate's guest and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 沛中豪傑吏聞令有重客，皆往賀。

translations.literal: The Pei middle powerful officials and clerks heard the magistrate had an important guest, all went to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: When the influential officials and clerks of Pei heard that the magistrate had an important guest, they all came to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 蕭何為主吏，主進，令諸大夫曰：「進不滿千錢，坐之堂下。」

translations.literal: Xiao He was the chief clerk, took charge of receiving, commanded the various officials saying: "Those who advance less than one thousand cash, seat them below the hall."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He served as chief clerk and was in charge of receiving guests. He instructed the other officials: "Those who present less than one thousand cash should be seated below the hall."

sentences.zh: 高祖為亭長，素易諸吏，乃紿為謁曰「賀錢萬」，實不持一錢。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was pavilion chief, usually casual with the officials, then deceived to make the announcement saying "Congratulatory money ten thousand," in reality he did not bring a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu had always treated the officials lightly. He deceived them by having the announcement read "Congratulatory gift: ten thousand cash," though in fact he did not bring a single coin.

sentences.zh: 謁入，呂公大驚，起，迎之門。

translations.literal: The announcement entered, Lü Gong was greatly startled, rose, welcomed him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the announcement was read, Lü Gong was greatly startled. He rose and went out to welcome him at the gate.

sentences.zh: 呂公者，好相人，見高祖狀貌，因重敬之，引入坐上坐。

translations.literal: Lü Gong was good at physiognomy, saw the Supreme Ancestor's appearance, because of this greatly respected him, led him in to sit in the seat of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong was skilled in reading faces. When he saw Emperor Gaozu's appearance, he was greatly impressed and led him inside to be seated in the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 蕭何曰：「劉季固多大言，少成事。」

translations.literal: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji indeed makes many big claims, accomplishes few matters."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji certainly talks big but accomplishes little."

sentences.zh: 高祖因狎侮諸客，遂坐上坐，無所詘。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor because of this treated the various guests with familiarity and insult, then sat in the seat of honor, was not humble in any way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took advantage of this to treat all the guests with casual familiarity and even insult them. He sat in the place of honor without showing any humility.

sentences.zh: 酒闌，呂公因目固留高祖。

translations.literal: The wine came to an end, Lü Gong because of this gave meaningful looks and firmly kept the Supreme Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: As the banquet ended, Lü Gong signaled insistently to keep Emperor Gaozu there.

sentences.zh: 竟酒，後。

translations.literal: The wine banquet ended, afterwards.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was finished, Gaozu stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 呂公曰：「臣少好相人，相人多矣，無如季相，願季自愛。

translations.literal: Lü Gong said: "I from youth favored physiognomy, have read many people's faces, none like Ji's appearance, wish Ji to take care of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong said: "Since I was young, I've enjoyed reading faces. I've read many people's faces, but none compare to Ji's. I hope Ji takes good care of himself.

sentences.zh: 臣有息女，願為箕帚妾。」

translations.literal: I have a young daughter, wish to make her Ji's broom and dustpan servant."
translations.idiomatic: I have a young daughter and wish to make her Ji's humble servant."

sentences.zh: 酒罷，呂媼怒呂公曰：「公始常欲奇此女，與貴人。

translations.literal: The wine ended, Lü Po became angry at Lü Gong and said: "You at first constantly wished to treat this daughter as exceptional, to match her with a noble person.
translations.idiomatic: After the wine ended, Lü Po angrily confronted Lü Gong: "You always said this daughter was exceptional and should marry someone noble.

sentences.zh: 沛令善公，求之不與，何自妄許與劉季？」

translations.literal: The Pei magistrate was friendly with you, requested her and you did not give, why now rashly promise her to Liu Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Pei was your friend and asked for her, but you wouldn't give her. Why are you now rashly promising her to Liu Ji?"

sentences.zh: 呂公曰：「此非兒女子所知。」

translations.literal: Lü Gong said: "This is not something that children and women understand."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong replied: "This is not something that mere children and women can understand."

sentences.zh: 卒與高祖。

translations.literal: In the end he married with the Supreme Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, she married Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 呂公女即呂后也，生孝惠帝、魯元公主。

translations.literal: Lü Gong's daughter was namely Empress Lü, gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: This daughter of Lü Gong would become Empress Lü. She gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗告歸之田。

translations.literal: The Supreme Ancestor once requested leave to return to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Once, Emperor Gaozu requested leave to return to his fields.

sentences.zh: 呂后與兩子居田中，有一老父過請飲，呂后因餔之。

translations.literal: Empress Lü and the two children resided in the fields, there was an old father who passed by requesting drink, Empress Lü because of this fed him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü lived in the countryside with their two children. An old man passed by and asked for a drink. Empress Lü fed him.

sentences.zh: 老父相后曰：「夫人天下貴人也。」

translations.literal: The old father read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame is a noble person of the world."
translations.idiomatic: The old man read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame, you are a noble person of the world."

sentences.zh: 令相兩子，見孝惠帝，曰：「夫人所以貴者，乃此男也。」

translations.literal: She had him read the faces of the two children; when he saw Emperor Xiaohui, he said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."
translations.idiomatic: He had him read the faces of the two children. When he saw Emperor Xiaohui, he said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."

sentences.zh: 相魯元公主，亦皆貴。

translations.literal: He read Princess Lu Yuan's face, all were noble.
translations.idiomatic: He read Princess Lu Yuan's face as well - all were noble.

sentences.zh: 老父已去，高祖適從旁舍來，呂后具言客有過，相我子母皆大貴。

translations.literal: The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and her children—all were greatly noble.
translations.idiomatic: The old man had already left. Emperor Gaozu had just returned from a neighboring house. Empress Lü told him everything: a guest had passed by and read the faces of her, the children, and her mother—they were all greatly noble.

sentences.zh: 高祖問，曰：「未遠。」

translations.literal: Gaozu asked, said: 'Not far.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu asked where the old man had gone. She said, "Not far."

sentences.zh: 乃追及，問老父。

translations.literal: Then pursued and caught up, questioned the old father.
translations.idiomatic: So he pursued and caught up with him, asking the old man.

sentences.zh: 老父曰：「鄉者夫人兒子皆以君，君相貴不可言。」

translations.literal: The old father said: 'Just now, madam and the children were all judged noble because of you; your features show nobility beyond words.'
translations.idiomatic: The old man said: "Just now, Madame and the children all take after you. Your appearance shows nobility beyond words."

sentences.zh: 高祖乃謝曰：「誠如父言，不敢忘德。」

translations.literal: Gaozu then thanked saying: 'Truly as father says, do not dare forget the kindness.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu then thanked him and said: "If what you say is true, I won't forget your kindness."

sentences.zh: 及高祖貴，遂不知老父處。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became noble, then did not know the old father's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu rose to power, he could no longer find the old man.

sentences.zh: 高祖為亭長，乃鲈竹皮為冠，令求盜之薛治，時時冠之，及貴常冠，所謂「劉氏冠」也。

translations.literal: While Gaozu was pavilion chief, he made a cap of bamboo sheathing; he was ordered to pursue bandits in the Xue district and wore it from time to time; after he rose high he still wore it constantly—this is what is called the "Liu family cap."
translations.idiomatic: While he was pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu made a cap of bamboo sheathing. When he was sent to pursue bandits in the Xue district he wore it from time to time, and after he rose high he still wore it constantly. This is what was called the "Liu family cap."

sentences.zh: 高祖以亭長為縣送徒驪山，徒多道亡。

translations.literal: Gaozu as pavilion chief was ordered by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li, the convicts many fled on the road.
translations.idiomatic: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu was assigned by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li. Many of the convicts fled along the road.

sentences.zh: 自度比至皆亡之，到豐西澤中亭，止飲，夜皆解縱所送徒。

translations.literal: He estimated that by the time he arrived all would have fled, arrived at the pavilion in the western marshes of Feng, stopped to drink, at night all released the convicts he was escorting.
translations.idiomatic: He reckoned that by the time they arrived all would have fled anyway. When they reached the pavilion in the western marsh at Feng, he stopped to drink. At night he released all the convicts he was escorting.

translations.literal: He said, “
translations.idiomatic: He said, “

sentences.zh: 公等皆去，吾亦從此逝矣！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen all go, I also from here depart!'
translations.idiomatic: You all go ahead. I'll take my leave from here too!"

sentences.zh: 徒中壯士願從諸十餘人。

translations.literal: Among the convicts the strong men who wished to follow were more than ten people.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten strong men among the convicts wished to follow him.

sentences.zh: 高祖被酒，夜徑澤中，令一人行前。

translations.literal: Gaozu was drunk, at night went straight through the marshes, ordered one person to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and at night went directly through the marsh, ordering one man to go ahead.

sentences.zh: 行前者還報曰：「

translations.literal: The one who went ahead returned and reported, “
translations.idiomatic: The man sent ahead came back and reported, “

sentences.zh: 前有大蛇當徑，願還。」

translations.literal: Ahead there is a large snake blocking the path, wish to turn back.'
translations.idiomatic: There is a large snake blocking the path ahead. We should turn back."

sentences.zh: 高祖醉，曰：「壯士行，何畏！」

translations.literal: Gaozu was drunk, said: 'A brave man walks forward, what is there to fear!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "A brave man walks on. What is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 乃前，拔劍斬蛇。

translations.literal: Then went forward, drew sword and cut the snake.
translations.idiomatic: So he went forward and drew his sword to cut the snake.

sentences.zh: 蛇分為兩，道開。

translations.literal: The snake divided into two, the path opened.
translations.idiomatic: The snake split into two, and the path opened.

sentences.zh: 行數里，醉困臥。

translations.literal: Walked several li, drunk and weary lay down.
translations.idiomatic: He walked several li, then lay down drunk and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 後人來至蛇所，有一老嫗夜哭。

translations.literal: Later people came to the snake's location, there was an old woman crying at night.
translations.idiomatic: Later people came to the place where the snake was, and there was an old woman crying at night.

sentences.zh: 人問嫗何哭，嫗曰：「人殺吾子。」

translations.literal: People asked the old woman why she cried, the old woman said: 'A person killed my son.'
translations.idiomatic: People asked the old woman why she was crying. The old woman said: "Someone killed my son."

sentences.zh: 人曰：「嫗子何為見殺？」

translations.literal: People said: 'Old woman's son why was he killed?'
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Why was your son killed?"

sentences.zh: 嫗曰：「吾子，白帝子也，化為蛇，當道，今者赤帝子斬之，故哭。」

translations.literal: Old woman said: 'My son was the son of the White Emperor, transformed into a snake, blocked the path, now the son of the Red Emperor cut him, therefore cry.'
translations.idiomatic: The old woman said: "My son was the son of the White Emperor. He transformed into a snake and blocked the road. Just now, the son of the Red Emperor cut him down. That's why I'm crying."

sentences.zh: 人乃以嫗為不誠，欲苦之，嫗因忽不見。

translations.literal: People then considered the old woman not sincere, wished to harm her, the old woman thus suddenly disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: The men thought the old woman was lying and wanted to punish her, but she suddenly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 後人至，高祖覺。

translations.literal: Later people arrived, Gaozu awoke.
translations.idiomatic: Later people arrived, and Emperor Gaozu woke up.

sentences.zh: 告高祖，高祖乃心獨喜，自負。

translations.literal: Told Gaozu, Gaozu then in his heart alone rejoiced, considered himself superior.
translations.idiomatic: They told Emperor Gaozu, who was secretly delighted and grew confident in himself.

sentences.zh: 諸從者日益畏之。

translations.literal: The various followers increasingly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers grew increasingly fearful of him.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇帝嘗曰「東南有天子氣」，於是東游以猒當之。

translations.literal: Qin Shi Huang often said 'there is emperor aura in the southeast', therefore traveled east to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang once said: "There is imperial aura in the southeast." So he traveled east to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 高祖隱於芒、碭山澤間，呂后與人俱求，常得之。

translations.literal: Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang, Empress Lu and others together sought him, constantly found him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang. Empress Lü and others searched for him together and always found him.

sentences.zh: 高祖怪問之。

translations.literal: Gaozu strangely questioned her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was surprised and asked how.

sentences.zh: 呂后曰：「季所居上常有雲氣，故從往常得季。」

translations.literal: Empress Lu said: 'Where Ji resides above constantly has cloud aura, therefore following it constantly finds Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü said: "There are always clouds above where you stay. That's why we can always find you by following them."

sentences.zh: 高祖又喜。

translations.literal: Gaozu again was happy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted once more.

sentences.zh: 沛中子弟或聞之，多欲附者矣。

translations.literal: Some of the youths in Pei heard of it, many wished to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some young men from Pei heard about this and many wished to join him.

sentences.zh: 秦二世元年秋七月，陳涉起蘄，至陳，自立為楚王，遣武臣、張耳、陳餘略趙地。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi, reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi. He reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 八月，武臣自立為趙王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wu Chen set himself up as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wu Chen set himself up as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 郡縣多殺長吏以應涉。

translations.literal: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in order to respond to Chen She.
translations.idiomatic: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in response to Chen She.

sentences.zh: 九月，沛令欲以沛應之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the magistrate of Pei wanted to respond to him with Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the magistrate of Pei wanted Pei to join the uprising in response to him.

sentences.zh: 掾、主吏蕭何、曹參曰：「君為秦吏，今欲背之，帥沛子弟，恐不聽。

translations.literal: The assistants and chief clerks Xiao He and Cao Can said, "You are an official of Qin. If you now wish to turn your back on it and lead the young men of Pei, we fear they will not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The assistants and chief clerks Xiao He and Cao Can said, "You are an official of Qin. If you now turn against it and try to lead the young men of Pei, we fear they will not obey.

sentences.zh: 願君召諸亡在外者，可得數百人，因以劫眾，眾不敢不聽。」

translations.literal: We hope that you will summon those fugitives who are outside; you can get several hundred men, and by using them to overawe the people, the people will not dare not to obey."
translations.idiomatic: We hope you will summon those fugitives who are outside. You can get several hundred men, and by using them to overawe the people, the people will not dare disobey."

sentences.zh: 乃令樊噲召高祖。

translations.literal: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖之眾已數百人矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 於是樊噲從高祖來。

translations.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and came.
translations.idiomatic: So Fan Kuai came to follow Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 沛令後悔，恐其有變，乃閉城城守，欲誅蕭、曹。

translations.literal: The Pei magistrate afterward regretted, feared there would be change, then closed the city gates and defended, wished to execute Xiao and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Pei later regretted it and feared there would be trouble, so he closed the city gates and defended, wanting to execute Xiao and Cao.

sentences.zh: 蕭、曹恐，踰城保高祖。

translations.literal: Xiao and Cao feared, climbed over the wall to protect Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao and Cao were afraid, so they climbed over the wall to join Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃書帛射城上，與沛父老曰：「天下同苦秦久矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, telling the Pei elders: 'The world together has suffered under Qin for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, saying to the elders of Pei: "All under heaven have suffered under Qin for a long time.

sentences.zh: 今父老雖為沛令守，諸侯並起，今屠沛。

translations.literal: Now although elders defend for the Pei magistrate, the feudal lords all rise, now will slaughter Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Now although you elders are defending for the magistrate of Pei, the feudal lords are all rising up, and Pei will be massacred.

sentences.zh: 沛今共誅令，擇可立立之，以應諸侯，即室家完。

translations.literal: Pei now together execute the magistrate, choose suitable one and establish him, to respond to the feudal lords, then families complete.
translations.idiomatic: If Pei now joins together to execute the magistrate and chooses someone worthy to establish as leader to respond to the feudal lords, then your families will be safe.

sentences.zh: 不然，父子俱屠，無為也。」

translations.literal: If not, fathers and sons together slaughtered, useless.'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, fathers and sons will all be massacred together. There will be no benefit."

sentences.zh: 父老乃帥子弟共殺沛令，開城門迎高祖，欲以為沛令。

translations.literal: The elders then led the young men together to kill the Pei magistrate, opened the city gates to welcome Gaozu, wished to make him Pei magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The elders then led the young men together to kill the magistrate of Pei, opened the city gates to welcome Emperor Gaozu, and wanted to make him magistrate of Pei.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「天下方擾，諸侯並起，令置將不善，一敗塗地。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'The world is currently in chaos, feudal lords all rise, if the magistrate appoints generals poorly, one defeat and all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: "The world is in chaos right now, with feudal lords rising up everywhere. If you appoint a commander who is not capable, one defeat will ruin everything.

sentences.zh: 吾非敢自愛，恐能薄，不能完父兄子弟。

translations.literal: I do not dare cherish myself, fear my abilities are meager, cannot protect fathers, elder brothers, younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: I'm not trying to protect myself. I'm afraid my abilities are weak and I cannot protect the fathers, brothers, and children.

sentences.zh: 此大事，願吏擇可者。」

translations.literal: This is a great matter, wish officials choose suitable one.'
translations.idiomatic: This is a major matter. I hope the officials will choose someone suitable."

sentences.zh: 蕭、曹等皆文吏，自愛，恐事不就，後秦種族其家，盡讓高祖。

translations.literal: Xiao, Cao and others all were civil officials, cherished themselves, feared the matter would not succeed, afterward Qin would exterminate their families, all yielded to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, Cao, and the others were all civil officials who cherished themselves. They feared that if things didn't succeed, Qin would exterminate their families, so they all yielded to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 諸父老皆曰：「平生所聞劉季奇怪，當貴，且卜筮之，莫如劉季最吉。」

translations.literal: All the elders said: 'In our lives we have heard Liu Ji is strange and extraordinary, should be noble, moreover divining it, none is more auspicious than Liu Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: All the elders said: "In our lifetimes we have heard that Liu Ji is strange and marked for nobility. Moreover, when we divined on it, none was more auspicious than Liu Ji."

sentences.zh: 高祖數讓。

translations.literal: Gaozu repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu declined repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 眾莫肯為，高祖乃立為沛公。

translations.literal: The crowd none would do it, Gaozu then was established as Pei Gong.
translations.idiomatic: No one else was willing to take it, so Emperor Gaozu was established as Lord of Pei.

sentences.zh: 祠黃帝，祭蚩尤於沛廷，而釁鼓旗。

translations.literal: Sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor, offered sacrifice to Chi You in the Pei court, and smeared blood on drums and flags.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor and made offerings to Chiyou in the Pei court, and smeared blood on the drums and flags.

sentences.zh: 幟皆赤，由所殺蛇白帝子，所殺者赤帝子故也。

translations.literal: The banners all red, because the killed snake was White Emperor's son, the one who killed was Red Emperor's son therefore.
translations.idiomatic: All the banners were red, because the snake he killed was the son of the White Emperor, and the one who killed it was the son of the Red Emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是少年豪吏如蕭、曹、樊噲等皆為收沛子弟，得三千人。

translations.literal: Therefore young heroic officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai and others all recruited Pei youths, got three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: So the young brave officials like Xiao, Cao, Fan Kuai, and others all recruited young men from Pei and gathered three thousand.

sentences.zh: 是月，項梁與兄子羽起吳。

translations.literal: This month, Xiang Liang and his brother's son Yu rose in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In this month, Xiang Liang and his brother's son Yu rose up in Wu.

sentences.zh: 田儋與從弟榮、橫起齊，自立為齊王。

translations.literal: Tian Dan and his younger cousins Rong, Heng rose in Qi, self-established as Qi King.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan and his younger brothers Rong and Heng rose up in Qi, establishing themselves as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 韓廣自立為燕王。

translations.literal: Han Guang self-established as Yan King.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang established himself as King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 魏咎自立為魏王。

translations.literal: Wei Jiu self-established as Wei King.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiu established himself as King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳涉之將周章西入關，至戲，秦將章邯距破之。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng's general Zhou Zhang entered the pass westward, arrived at Xi, Qin general Zhang Han resisted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She's general Zhou Zhang marched west into the pass and reached Xi, where Qin general Zhang Han opposed and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 秦二年十月，沛公攻胡陵、方與，還守豐。

translations.literal: Qin second year tenth month, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, returned to defend Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Qin, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, then returned to defend Feng.

sentences.zh: 秦泗川監平將兵圍豐。

translations.literal: Qin Sishui inspector Ping led troops to surround Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin governor of Si River Ping led troops to besiege Feng.

sentences.zh: 二日，出與戰，破之。

translations.literal: Two days, went out and fought with them, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: For two days they came out to battle and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 令雍齒守豐。

translations.literal: Ordered Yong Chi to defend Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yong Chi to defend Feng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，沛公引兵之薛。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xue.

sentences.zh: 秦泗川守壯兵敗於薛，走至戚，沛公左司馬得殺之。

translations.literal: Qin Sishui defender Zhuang's troops defeated at Xue, fled to Qi, Pei Gong's left marshal captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin governor of Si River Zhuang was defeated at Xue and fled to Qi, where Pei Gong's left commander Sima De killed him.

sentences.zh: 沛公還軍亢父，至方與。

translations.literal: Pei Gong returned his army to Kang Fu, arrived at Fang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong returned his army to Kangfu and arrived at Fang Yu.

sentences.zh: 趙王武臣為其將所殺。

translations.literal: Zhao King wuchen day was killed by his general.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhao was killed by his own general.

sentences.zh: 十二月，楚王陳涉為其御莊賈所殺。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Chu King Chen Sheng was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, King Chen She of Chu was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.

sentences.zh: 魏人周市略地豐沛，使人謂雍齒曰：「豐，故梁徙也，今魏地已定者數十城。

translations.literal: Wei person Zhou Shi conquered territory Feng Pei, sent person to tell Yong Chi: 'Feng was originally Liang migrants, now Wei territory already settled dozens of cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei man Zhou Shi seized territory in Feng and Pei, and sent someone to tell Yong Chi: "Feng was originally Liang territory, now Wei has already pacified dozens of cities.

sentences.zh: 齒今下魏，魏以齒為侯守豐；

translations.literal: Chi now submit to Wei, Wei will make Chi marquis to guard Feng;
translations.idiomatic: If Chi now submits to Wei, Wei will make Chi a marquess to guard Feng;

sentences.zh: 不下，且屠豐。」

translations.literal: if not submit, then will slaughter Feng.'
translations.idiomatic: if he doesn't submit, Wei will massacre Feng."

sentences.zh: 雍齒雅不欲屬沛公，及魏招之，即反為魏守豐。

translations.literal: Yong Chi usually did not wish to belong to Pei Gong, when Wei summoned him, immediately rebelled to guard Feng for Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Chi had long not wanted to serve Pei Gong, and when Wei summoned him, he immediately rebelled and defended Feng for Wei.

sentences.zh: 沛公攻豐，不能取。

translations.literal: Pei Gong attacked Feng, could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong attacked Feng but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 沛公還之沛，怨雍齒與豐子弟畔之。

translations.literal: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resented Yong Chi and the Feng youths rebelling against him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resentful that Yong Chi and the young men of Feng had rebelled against him.

sentences.zh: 正月，張耳等立趙後趙歇為趙王。

translations.literal: First month, Zhang Er and others established Zhao descendant Zhao Xie as Zhao King.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, Zhang Er and others established Zhao's former king Zhao Xie as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 東陽甯君、秦嘉立景駒為楚王，在留。

translations.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Qin Jia established Jing Ju as Chu King, at Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Qin Jia established Jing Ju as King of Chu, stationed at Liu.

sentences.zh: 沛公往從之，道得張良，遂與俱見景駒，請兵以攻豐。

translations.literal: Pei Gong went to follow them, on the road obtained Zhang Liang, then together went to see Jing Ju, requested troops to attack Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong went to join him, met Zhang Liang along the way, and together they went to see Jing Ju, requesting troops to attack Feng.

sentences.zh: 時章邯從陳，別將司馬镛將兵北定楚地，屠相，至碭。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Han came from Chen, separate general Sima Ni led troops north to pacify Chu territory, massacred Xiang, arrived at Dang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Zhang Han was pursuing Chen, while his deputy general Sima Yiou led troops north to pacify Chu territory, massacring Xiang and reaching Dang.

sentences.zh: 東陽甯君、沛公引兵西，與戰蕭西，不利，還收兵聚留。

translations.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Pei Gong led troops west, fought battle at Xiao west, unfavorable, returned gathered troops at Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Pei Gong led troops west and battled west of Xiao, but were unsuccessful, so they retreated and gathered troops at Liu.

sentences.zh: 二月，攻碭，三日拔之。

translations.literal: Second month, attacked Dang, three days captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, they attacked Dang and captured it after three days.

sentences.zh: 收碭兵，得六千人，與故合九千人。

translations.literal: Recruited Dang troops, got six thousand, combined with original made nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited troops from Dang, getting six thousand men, and together with the previous troops made nine thousand.

sentences.zh: 三月，攻下邑，拔之。

translations.literal: Third month, attacked Xiayi, captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, they attacked Xiayi and captured it.

sentences.zh: 還擊豐，不下。

translations.literal: Returned to attack Feng, could not capture.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to attack Feng, but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 四月，項梁擊殺景駒、秦嘉，止薛，沛公往見之。

translations.literal: Fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju, Qin Jia, stopped at Xue, Pei Gong went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju and Qin Jia, then stopped at Xue. Pei Gong went to see him.

sentences.zh: 項梁益沛公卒五千人，五大夫將十人。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops five thousand, Grand Master generals ten people.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops by five thousand men and ten generals of the rank of Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 沛公還，引兵攻豐，拔之。

translations.literal: Pei Gong returned, led troops to attack Feng, captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong returned and led troops to attack Feng, capturing it.

sentences.zh: 雍齒奔魏。

translations.literal: Yong Chi fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Chi fled to the state of Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，項羽拔襄城還。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Xiang Yu captured Xiangcheng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xiang Yu captured Xiangcheng and returned.

sentences.zh: 項梁盡召別將。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang completely summoned the separate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang summoned all his deputy generals.

sentences.zh: 六月，沛公如薛，與項梁共立楚懷王孫心為楚懷王。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue, together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as Chu King Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue and together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as King Huai of Chu.

sentences.zh: 章邯破殺魏王咎、齊王田儋於臨濟。

translations.literal: Zhang Han defeated and killed Wei King Jiu, Qi King Tian Dan at Linji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han defeated and killed King Jiu of Wei and King Tian Dan of Qi at Linji.

sentences.zh: 七月，大霖雨。

translations.literal: Seventh month, great continuous rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, there was heavy continuous rain.

sentences.zh: 沛公攻亢父。

translations.literal: Pei Gong attacked Kang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong attacked Kangfu.

sentences.zh: 章邯圍田榮於東阿。

translations.literal: Zhang Han besieged Tian Rong at Dong'a.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han besieged Tian Rong at Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 沛公與項梁共救田榮，大破章邯東阿。

translations.literal: Pei Gong together with Xiang Liang rescued Tian Rong, greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'a.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong and Xiang Liang together went to rescue Tian Rong and greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 田榮歸，沛公、項羽追北，至城陽，攻屠其城。

translations.literal: Tian Rong returned, Pei Gong, Xiang Yu pursued north, arrived at Chengyang, attacked and slaughtered its city.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong returned. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu pursued the defeated enemy north to Chengyang and attacked, massacring the population of the city.

sentences.zh: 軍濮陽東，復與章邯戰，又破之。

translations.literal: Camped east of Puyang, again fought with Zhang Han, again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped east of Puyang and again battled Zhang Han, defeating him once more.

sentences.zh: 章邯復振，守濮陽，環水。

translations.literal: Zhang Han again recovered, defended Puyang, surrounded by water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han recovered his strength and defended Puyang, surrounding it with water.

sentences.zh: 沛公、項羽去攻定陶。

translations.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 八月，田榮立田儋子市為齊王。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Tian Rong established Tian Dan's son Shi as Qi King.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tian Rong established Tian Dan's son Shi as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 定陶未下，沛公與項羽西略地至雍丘，與秦軍戰，大敗之，斬三川守李由。

translations.literal: Dingtao not yet fallen, Pei Gong together with Xiang Yu west conquered territory to Yongqiu, fought with Qin army, greatly defeated them, beheaded Sanchuan defender Li You.
translations.idiomatic: Dingtao had not yet fallen. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu marched west to seize territory as far as Yongqiu, where they battled Qin troops and greatly defeated them, beheading the governor of Sanchuan, Li You.

sentences.zh: 還攻外黃，外黃未下。

translations.literal: Returned to attack Waihuang, Waihuang did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to attack Waihuang, but Waihuang did not fall.

sentences.zh: 項梁再破秦軍，有驕色。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang again defeated Qin army, had arrogant appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang defeated the Qin army again and showed arrogant bearing.

sentences.zh: 宋義諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Song Yi advised, did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi advised against it, but Xiang Liang did not listen.

sentences.zh: 秦益章邯兵。

translations.literal: Qin increased Zhang Han's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qin reinforced Zhang Han's army.

sentences.zh: 九月，章邯夜銜枚擊項梁定陶，大破之，殺項梁。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Zhang Han night held wooden gag attacked Xiang Liang at Dingtao, greatly defeated him, killed Xiang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhang Han bit on wooden sticks and attacked Xiang Liang at Dingtao by night, greatly defeating him and killing Xiang Liang.

sentences.zh: 時連雨自七月至九月。

translations.literal: At this time continuous rain from seventh month to ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: At this time there was continuous rain from the seventh month until the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 沛公、項羽方攻陳留，聞梁死，士卒恐，乃與將軍呂臣引兵而東，徙懷王自盱台都彭城。

translations.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu just attacking Chenliu, heard Liang died, soldiers afraid, then together with general Lu Chen led troops east, moved King Huai from Xutai capital to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu were attacking Chenliu when they heard of Liang's death. The soldiers were terrified, so they joined with General Lü Chen and led troops east, moving King Huai from Xutai to Pengcheng as the capital.

sentences.zh: 呂臣軍彭城東，項羽軍彭城西，沛公軍碭。

translations.literal: Lu Chen's army east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, Pei Gong's army at Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chen's army was stationed east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, and Pei Gong's army at Dang.

sentences.zh: 魏咎弟豹自立為魏王。

translations.literal: Wei Jiu's younger brother Bao self-established as Wei King.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiu's younger brother Bao established himself as King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後九月，懷王并呂臣、項羽軍自將之。

translations.literal: After ninth month, King Huai merged Lu Chen, Xiang Yu's armies and personally led them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month afterward, King Huai combined Lü Chen and Xiang Yu's armies and personally took command.

sentences.zh: 以沛公為碭郡長，封武安侯，將碭郡兵。

translations.literal: Made Pei Gong Dang commandery chief, sealed as Marquis of Wuan, led Dang commandery troops.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuan, and put him in command of Dang commandery troops.

sentences.zh: 以羽為魯公，封長安侯，呂臣為司徒，其父呂青為令尹。

translations.literal: Made Yu Duke of Lu, sealed as Marquis of Chang'an, Lu Chen as Minister of the Masses, his father Lu Qing as Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yu as Duke of Lu and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chang'an. Lü Chen became Minister of Works, and his father Lü Qing became Prime Minister.

sentences.zh: 章邯已破項梁，以為楚地兵不足憂，乃渡河北擊趙王歇，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Han having defeated Xiang Liang, thought Chu territory troops not worth worrying about, then crossed north of Yellow River attacked Zhao King Xie, greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han had already defeated Xiang Liang and thought that the Chu region's troops were not worth worrying about, so he crossed north of the Yellow River to attack King Xie of Zhao, greatly defeating him.

sentences.zh: 歇保鉅鹿城，秦將王離圍之。

translations.literal: Xie defended Julu city, Qin general Wang Li besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie defended the city of Julu, where Qin general Wang Li besieged him.

sentences.zh: 趙數請救，懷王乃以宋義為上將，項羽為次將，范增為末將，北救趙。

translations.literal: Zhao repeatedly requested rescue, King Huai then made Song Yi supreme general, Xiang Yu deputy general, Fan Zeng rear general, north to rescue Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao repeatedly requested rescue, so King Huai appointed Song Yi as supreme commander, Xiang Yu as deputy commander, and Fan Zeng as rear commander, to go north and rescue Zhao.

sentences.zh: 初，懷王與諸將約，先入定關中者王之。

translations.literal: Originally, King Huai made agreement with various generals, the first to enter and pacify Guanzhong would be made king there.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, King Huai had made an agreement with the generals that whoever first entered and pacified Guanzhong would be made king of it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，秦兵彊，常乘勝逐北，諸將莫利先入關。

translations.literal: At this time, Qin troops strong, constantly took advantage of victory pursued retreating enemy, various generals none saw benefit in entering pass first.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Qin troops were strong and often took advantage of victories to pursue defeated enemies. None of the generals saw benefit in being the first to enter the pass.

sentences.zh: 獨羽怨秦破項梁，奮勢，願與沛公西入關。

translations.literal: Only Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang, exerted his influence, wished to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiang Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang and was eager to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.

sentences.zh: 懷王諸老將皆曰：「項羽為人慓悍禍賊，嘗攻襄城，襄城無唣類，所過無不殘滅。

translations.literal: King Huai's various old generals all said: 'Xiang Yu as a person is fierce and violent, a calamitous bandit, once attacked Xiangcheng, Xiangcheng had no survivors, wherever he passed nothing was not completely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai's veteran generals all said: "Xiang Yu is fierce and violent, a man of disaster. He once attacked Xiangcheng, leaving no survivors in Xiangcheng. Wherever he passes, nothing is left undestroyed.

sentences.zh: 且楚數進取，前陳王、項梁皆敗，不如更遣長者扶義而西，告諭秦父兄。

translations.literal: Moreover Chu repeatedly advanced and took, previously King Chen, Xiang Liang all defeated, not as good as again send elder who upholds righteousness west, inform and persuade Qin fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Chu has repeatedly advanced but the former King Chen and Xiang Liang both failed. It would be better to send an elder who upholds righteousness to go west and inform the fathers and brothers of Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦父兄苦其主久矣，今誠得長者往，毋侵暴，宜可下。

translations.literal: Qin fathers and elder brothers have suffered under their ruler for a long time, now truly if elder goes, do not invade violently, should be able to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The fathers and brothers of Qin have suffered under their ruler for a long time. Now if we truly send an elder, without invasion or violence, the region should submit.

sentences.zh: 項羽不可遣，獨沛公素寬大長者。」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu cannot be sent, only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and elder.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu should not be sent. Only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and an elder."

sentences.zh: 卒不許羽，而遣沛公西收陳王、項梁散卒。

translations.literal: In the end did not permit Yu, instead sent Pei Gong west to gather King Chen, Xiang Liang's scattered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they did not permit Xiang Yu, but sent Pei Gong west to gather the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang.

sentences.zh: 乃道碭至陽城與杠里，攻秦軍壁，破其二軍。

translations.literal: Then took the Dang road to Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin army fortifications, broke their two armies.
translations.idiomatic: So he went by way of Dang to Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin army fortifications, and broke two of their armies.

sentences.zh: 秦三年十月，齊將田都畔田榮，將兵助項羽救趙。

translations.literal: Qin third year tenth month, Qi general Tian Du rebelled against Tian Rong, led troops to assist Xiang Yu rescue Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Qin, Qi general Tian Du rebelled against Tian Rong and led troops to help Xiang Yu rescue Zhao.

sentences.zh: 沛公攻破東郡尉於成武。

translations.literal: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dongjun prefect at Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dong commandery commandant at Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，項羽殺宋義，并其兵渡河，自立為上將軍，諸將黥布等皆屬。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Xiang Yu killed Song Yi, merged his troops crossed the river, self-established as supreme general, various generals Ying Bu and others all belonged to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xiang Yu killed Song Yi and took his troops, crossed the river, and established himself as supreme commander. Generals like Ying Bu and others all came under his command.

sentences.zh: 十二月，沛公引兵至栗，遇剛武侯，奪其軍四千餘人，并之，與魏將皇欣、武滿軍合，攻秦軍，破之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li, encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized his army more than four thousand people, merged them, combined with Wei generals Huang Xin, Wu Man armies, attacked Qin army, defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li and encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized over four thousand of his men, and combined them. He joined with Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man's army and attacked Qin troops, defeating them.

sentences.zh: 故齊王建孫田安下濟北，從項羽救趙。

translations.literal: Former Qi King Jian's grandson Tian An went down north of Ji, followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qi King Jian's grandson Tian An captured Jibei and followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao.

sentences.zh: 羽大破秦軍鉅鹿下，虜王離，走章邯。

translations.literal: Yu greatly defeated Qin army below Julu, captured Wang Li, routed Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu greatly defeated the Qin army at Julu, captured Wang Li, and drove away Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 二月，沛公從碭北攻昌邑，遇彭越。

translations.literal: Second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi, encountered Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi and encountered Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 越助攻昌邑，未下。

translations.literal: Yue helped attack Changyi, did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yue helped attack Changyi, but it did not fall.

sentences.zh: 沛公西過高陽，酈食其為里監門，曰：「諸將過此者多，吾視沛公大度。」

translations.literal: Pei Gong west passed Gaoyang, Li Yiji was village gatekeeper, said: 'Various generals who passed this place many, I observe Pei Gong has great magnanimity.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong passed west through Gaoyang. Li Yiji was the village gatekeeper and said: "Many generals have passed through here. I can see that Pei Gong has great magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 乃求見沛公。

translations.literal: Then requested to see Pei Gong.
translations.idiomatic: So he sought to see Pei Gong.

sentences.zh: 沛公方踞床，使兩女子洗。

translations.literal: Pei Gong just then squatting on bed, made two women wash.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong was sitting cross-legged on a bed, having two women wash his feet.

sentences.zh: 酈生不拜，長揖曰：「足下必欲誅無道秦，不宜踞見長者。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng did not bow, gave long bow said: 'Your excellency certainly wishes to execute unrighteous Qin, should not lounge to see elders.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng did not bow but gave a deep bow and said: "If you truly wish to execute the tyrannical Qin, you should not sit cross-legged when receiving elders."

sentences.zh: 於是沛公起，攝衣謝之，延上坐。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pei Gong rose, gathered clothes thanked him, invited to upper seat.
translations.idiomatic: So Pei Gong rose, straightened his clothes, and apologized. He invited him to sit in the honored position.

sentences.zh: 食其說沛公襲陳留。

translations.literal: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.

sentences.zh: 沛公以為廣野君，以其弟商為將，將陳留兵。

translations.literal: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.

sentences.zh: 三月，攻開封，未拔。

translations.literal: In the third month, they attacked Kaifeng but failed to capture it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, they attacked Kaifeng but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 西與秦將楊熊會戰白馬，又戰曲遇東，大破之。

translations.literal: They met Qin general Yang Xiong in battle at Baima to the west, and again at Quyu to the east, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: They met Qin general Yang Xiong in battle at Baima to the west, and again at Quyu to the east, greatly defeating him.

sentences.zh: 楊熊走之滎陽，二世使使斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang. The Second Emperor sent an envoy to execute him as a warning to others.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang. The Second Emperor sent an envoy to execute him as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 四月，南攻潁川，屠之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, they attacked Yingchuan to the south and massacred the population.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, they attacked Yingchuan to the south and massacred the population.

sentences.zh: 因張良遂略韓地。

translations.literal: Through Zhang Liang, they then seized the lands of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhang Liang, they then seized the lands of Han.

sentences.zh: 時趙別將司馬卬方欲渡河入關，沛公乃北攻平陰，絕河津。

translations.literal: At this time, the Zhao general Sima Ang was about to cross the river into the passes. Pei Gong attacked Beiyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Sima Ang, a separate Zhao general, was about to cross the Yellow River and enter the passes. Pei Gong therefore attacked Pingyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.

sentences.zh: 南，戰雒陽東，軍不利，從轘轅至陽城，收軍中馬騎。

translations.literal: To the south, they fought east of Luoyang. The battle went badly. They retreated from Huan Pass to Yangcheng and gathered cavalry from among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, they fought east of Luoyang, but the army fared badly. They withdrew from Huanyuan to Yangcheng and gathered the cavalry from the army.

sentences.zh: 六月，與南陽守齮戰犨東，大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they fought Nanyang governor Yin east of Chu, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, they fought Nanyang governor Yin east of Chu, greatly defeating him.

sentences.zh: 略南陽郡，南陽守走，保城守宛。

translations.literal: They seized Nanyang commandery. The Nanyang governor fled and defended the city of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Nanyang commandery. The Nanyang governor fled and defended the city of Wan.

sentences.zh: 沛公引兵過宛西。

translations.literal: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.

sentences.zh: 張良諫曰：「沛公雖欲急入關，秦兵尚眾，距險。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.

sentences.zh: 今不下宛，宛從後擊，彊秦在前，此危道也。」

translations.literal: If we do not take Wan now, Wan will attack from behind while the strong Qin face us ahead. This is a dangerous path."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take Wan now, Wan will attack from behind while the strong Qin face us ahead. This is a dangerous path."

sentences.zh: 於是沛公乃夜引軍從他道還，偃旗幟，遲明，圍宛城三匝。

translations.literal: So Pei Gong led his army back by another route at night, hid his banners, and at dawn surrounded Wan city three times.
translations.idiomatic: So Pei Gong led his army back by another route at night, hid his banners, and at dawn surrounded Wan city three times.

sentences.zh: 南陽守欲自剄，其舍人陳恢曰：「死未晚也。」

translations.literal: The Nanyang governor was about to commit suicide, but his aide Chen Hei said: "It is not yet time to die."
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang governor was about to commit suicide, but his aide Chen Hei said: "It is not yet time to die."

sentences.zh: 乃踰城見沛公，曰：「臣聞足下約先入咸陽者王之，今足下留守宛。

translations.literal: So he climbed over the wall to see Pei Gong and said: "I have heard that you promised to enfeoff as king whoever first entered Xianyang. Now you remain besieging Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore climbed over the wall to meet Pei Gong and said, "I have heard that you agreed that whoever first entered Xianyang would be made king there. Now you are staying here to besiege Wan.

sentences.zh: 宛郡縣連城數十，其吏民自以為降必死，故皆堅守乘城。

translations.literal: Wan commandery has dozens of walled cities connected together. Its officials and people believe they will certainly die if they surrender, so they all defend their walls firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Commandery has dozens of linked walled cities. Its officials and people believe that if they surrender they will certainly die, so they are all firmly defending the walls.

sentences.zh: 今足下盡日止攻，士死傷者必多；

translations.literal: If you continue attacking all day, your soldiers who die and are wounded will certainly be many;
translations.idiomatic: If you continue attacking all day, your soldiers who die and are wounded will certainly be many;

sentences.zh: 引兵去宛，宛必隨足下。

translations.literal: Lead your troops away from Wan, and Wan will certainly follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your troops away from Wan, and Wan will certainly follow you.

sentences.zh: 足下前則失咸陽之約，後有彊宛之患。

translations.literal: Ahead you lose the agreement about Xianyang, behind you have the danger of strong Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead you lose the agreement about Xianyang, behind you have the danger of strong Wan.

sentences.zh: 為足下計，莫若約降，封其守，因使止守，引其甲卒與之西。

translations.literal: For your sake, it would be better to make a treaty for surrender, enfeoff the governor, and then order him to remain as governor, leading his armored troops west with you.
translations.idiomatic: In planning for you, nothing would be better than agreeing on his surrender, enfeoffing its governor, and then ordering him to remain in charge while leading his armored troops west with you.

sentences.zh: 諸城未下者，聞聲爭開門而待足下，足下通行無所累。」

translations.literal: The cities that have not yet surrendered will hear of this and compete to open their gates waiting for you. You will pass through without hindrance."
translations.idiomatic: The cities not yet taken will hear of this and compete to open their gates to await you. You will pass through without obstruction."

sentences.zh: 沛公曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Pei Gong said: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong said: "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 七月，南陽守齮降，封為殷侯，封陳恢千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Nanyang governor Yin surrendered. He was enfeoffed as Lord Yin, and Chen Hei was enfeoffed with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Nanyang governor Yin surrendered. He was enfeoffed as Lord Yin, and Chen Hei was enfeoffed with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 引兵西，無不下者。

translations.literal: He led troops west, and there was no city that did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops west, and there was no city that did not surrender.

sentences.zh: 至丹水，高武侯鰓、襄侯王陵降。

translations.literal: He reached Danshui. Lord Gaowu Gai and Lord Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Danshui. Lord Gaowu Gai and Lord Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還攻胡陽，遇番君別將梅鋗，與偕攻析、酈，皆降。

translations.literal: Returning to attack Huyang, he encountered Fan Jun's separate general Mei Zhu, and together they attacked Xi and Li, all of which surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to attack Huyang, he encountered Fan Jun's separate general Mei Zhu, and together they attacked Xi and Li, all of which surrendered.

sentences.zh: 所過毋得鹵掠，秦民喜。

translations.literal: Wherever they passed, they did not plunder. The Qin people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they passed, they did not plunder. The Qin people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 遣魏人甯昌使秦。

translations.literal: He sent the Wei man Ning Chang as envoy to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Wei man Ning Chang as envoy to Qin.

sentences.zh: 是月章邯舉軍降項羽，羽以為雍王。

translations.literal: In this month, Zhang Han led his entire army to surrender to Xiang Yu, who enfeoffed him as King of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In this month, Zhang Han led his entire army to surrender to Xiang Yu, who enfeoffed him as King of Yong.

sentences.zh: 瑕丘申陽下河南。

translations.literal: Xiaqiu Shen Yang took Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqiu Shen Yang took Henan.

sentences.zh: 八月，沛公攻武關，入秦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Pei Gong attacked Wuguan and entered Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Pei Gong attacked Wuguan and entered Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦相趙高恐，乃殺二世，使人來，欲約分王關中，沛公不許。

translations.literal: Qin chancellor Zhao Gao became fearful, so he killed the Second Emperor and sent people to try to make a treaty to divide the kingship of Guanzhong. Pei Gong did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin Chancellor Zhao Gao became afraid, so he killed the Second Emperor and sent men to propose dividing Guanzhong into kingdoms. Pei Gong refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙高立二世兄子子嬰為秦王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhao Gao established the Second Emperor's younger brother Zi Ying as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhao Gao installed the Second Emperor's nephew Zi Ying as King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 子嬰誅滅趙高，遣將將兵距嶢關。

translations.literal: Zi Ying executed Zhao Gao and sent generals leading troops to defend Yao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Ying executed Zhao Gao and sent generals leading troops to defend Yao Pass.

sentences.zh: 沛公欲擊之，張良曰：「秦兵尚彊，未可輕。

translations.literal: Pei Gong wanted to attack them. Zhang Liang said: "The Qin troops are still strong. We cannot be careless.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong wanted to attack them. Zhang Liang said: "The Qin troops are still strong. We cannot be careless.

sentences.zh: 願先遣人益張旗幟於山上為疑兵，使酈食其、陸賈往說秦將，啗以利。」

translations.literal: I wish to first send people to increase banners on the mountains as feigned troops, and have Li Yiji and Lu Jia go persuade the Qin generals, enticing them with benefits."
translations.idiomatic: I would first send men to set up more banners on the mountains as decoy troops, while Li Yiji and Lu Jia go to persuade the Qin generals and entice them with advantage."

sentences.zh: 秦將果欲連和，沛公欲許之。

translations.literal: The Qin general indeed wanted to form an alliance. Pei Gong wanted to agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin general indeed wanted to form an alliance. Pei Gong wanted to agree.

sentences.zh: 張良曰：「此獨其將欲叛，恐其士卒不從，不如因其怠懈擊之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said: "This is only their general who wants to rebel. He fears his soldiers will not follow. It would be better to take advantage of their laxness and attack them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said: "Only their general wants to defect; he fears his soldiers will not follow. It would be better to strike while they are lax."

sentences.zh: 沛公引兵繞嶢關，踰蕢山，擊秦軍，大破之藍田南。

translations.literal: Pei Gong led his troops around Yao Pass, crossed Mount Qi, attacked the Qin army, and greatly defeated them south of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong led his troops around Yao Pass, crossed Mount Qi, attacked the Qin army, and greatly defeated them south of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 遂至藍田，又戰其北，秦兵大敗。

translations.literal: He then reached Lantian and fought again to its north. The Qin troops suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached Lantian and fought again to its north. The Qin troops suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 元年冬十月，五星聚于東井。

translations.literal: In the first year, in winter, in the tenth month, the five planets gathered at Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, in winter, in the tenth month, the five planets gathered at Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 沛公至霸上。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.

sentences.zh: 秦王子嬰素車白馬，係頸以組，封皇帝璽符節，降枳道旁。

translations.literal: Ziying, King of Qin, with a plain carriage and white horses, bound his neck with a cord, sealed up the emperor's seals, tallies, and credentials, and surrendered beside Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying, King of Qin, came with a plain carriage and white horses, bound his neck with a cord, sealed up the emperor's seals, tallies, and credentials, and surrendered beside Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 諸將或言誅秦王，沛公曰：「始懷王遣我，固以能寬容，且人已服降，殺之不祥。」

translations.literal: Some of the generals said to execute the King of Qin. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient; moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered, and to kill him would be inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Some of the generals said that the King of Qin should be executed. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient. Moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered; to kill him would be inauspicious."

sentences.zh: 乃以屬吏。

translations.literal: He then handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: He then handed him over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 遂西入咸陽，欲止宮休舍。

translations.literal: Then he entered Xianyang in the west and wanted to stop and rest in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then went west into Xianyang and wanted to stop and rest in the palace.

sentences.zh: 樊噲、張良諫，乃封秦重寶財物府庫，還軍霸上。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang remonstrated, so he sealed up Qin's important treasures, property, and treasuries, and returned the army to Bashang.

sentences.zh: 蕭何盡收秦丞相府圖籍文書。

translations.literal: Xiao He collected all the maps, registers, documents, and writings from the office of the Qin chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He collected all the maps, registers, documents, and writings from the office of the Qin chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，召諸縣豪桀曰：「父老苦秦苛法久矣，誹謗者族，耦語者棄市。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he summoned the leading men of the counties and said, "The elders have long suffered from Qin's harsh laws: those who criticized were exterminated by clan, and those who spoke together were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, he summoned the leading men of the counties and said, "The elders have long suffered from Qin's harsh laws: those who criticized the government were exterminated by clan, and those who spoke together were executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。

translations.literal: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 與父老約，法三章耳：殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。

translations.literal: I make an agreement with the elders: there are only three articles of law. Those who kill shall die; those who wound others and those who steal shall answer for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: I make this agreement with the elders: there will be only three articles of law. Those who kill shall die; those who wound others and those who steal shall answer for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 餘悉除去秦法。

translations.literal: All the rest of the Qin laws are removed.
translations.idiomatic: All the rest of the Qin laws are abolished.

sentences.zh: 吏民皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: Officials and people should all remain settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people should all remain settled as before.

sentences.zh: 凡吾所以來，為父兄除害，非有所侵暴，毋恐！

translations.literal: In general, the reason I have come is to remove harm for my fathers and elder brothers; it is not that there is any invasion or violence, so do not be afraid!
translations.idiomatic: The whole reason I have come is to remove harm for my fathers and elder brothers; I have not come to invade or oppress you, so do not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 且吾所以軍霸上，待諸侯至而定要束耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason I have stationed the army at Bashang is only to wait for the feudal lords to arrive and settle the agreements."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reason I have stationed the army at Bashang is only to wait for the feudal lords to arrive and settle the agreements."

sentences.zh: 乃使人與秦吏行至縣鄉邑告諭之。

translations.literal: He then sent people together with Qin officials to go to the counties, townships, and settlements and proclaim this to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent people together with Qin officials to go to the counties, townships, and settlements and proclaim this to them.

sentences.zh: 秦民大喜，爭持牛羊酒食獻享軍士。

translations.literal: The people of Qin were greatly delighted and vied in bringing cattle, sheep, wine, and food to present to and feast the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin were greatly delighted, and they vied with one another to bring cattle, sheep, wine, and food to present to the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 沛公讓不受，曰：「倉粟多，不欲費民。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei declined and would not accept them, saying, "There is much grain in the granaries, and I do not wish to burden the people."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei declined and would not accept them, saying, "There is abundant grain in the granaries, and I do not want to burden the people."

sentences.zh: 民又益喜，唯恐沛公不為秦王。

translations.literal: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 或說沛公曰：「秦富十倍天下，地形彊。

translations.literal: Someone advised Pei Gong: "Qin is ten times richer than the world, and its terrain is strong.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Pei Gong: "Qin is ten times as wealthy as all the rest of the realm, and its terrain is strong.

sentences.zh: 今聞章邯降項羽，羽號曰雍王，王關中。

translations.literal: Now we hear that Zhang Han has surrendered to Xiang Yu, who is titled King of Yong and rules Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear that Zhang Han has surrendered to Xiang Yu, who is titled King of Yong and rules Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 即來，沛公恐不得有此。

translations.literal: If he comes, Pei Gong fears he may not be able to hold this.
translations.idiomatic: If he comes, you may not be able to keep this.

sentences.zh: 可急使守函谷關，毋內諸侯軍，稍徵關中兵以自益，距之。」

translations.literal: We can urgently send people to defend Hangu Pass and not let the feudal lords' armies enter, gradually conscript Guanzhong troops to strengthen ourselves, and resist them."
translations.idiomatic: We should quickly send men to defend Hangu Pass, keep the armies of the feudal lords from entering, gradually call up Guanzhong troops to strengthen ourselves, and resist them."

sentences.zh: 沛公然其計，從之。

translations.literal: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.

sentences.zh: 十二月，項羽果帥諸侯兵欲西入關，關門閉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiang Yu indeed led the feudal lords' troops wanting to enter the passes to the west, but the pass gates were closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiang Yu did indeed lead the troops of the feudal lords westward to enter the passes, but the pass gates were closed.

sentences.zh: 聞沛公已定關中，羽大怒，使黥布等攻破函谷關，遂至戲下。

translations.literal: He heard that Pei Gong had already pacified Guanzhong. Xiang Yu was greatly angered and sent Ying Bu and others to break through Hangu Pass, then reached Xixia.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Pei Gong had already pacified Guanzhong, Xiang Yu was furious and sent Ying Bu and others to break through Hangu Pass, then advanced to Xi.

sentences.zh: 沛公左司馬曹毋傷聞羽怒，欲攻沛公，使人言羽曰：「沛公欲王關中，令子嬰相，珍寶盡有之。」

translations.literal: Pei Gong's left marshal Cao Wushang heard of Xiang Yu's anger and wanted to attack Pei Gong. He sent someone to tell Xiang Yu: "Pei Gong wants to become king of Guanzhong and has Zi Ying as chancellor, possessing all the precious treasures."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wushang, Pei Gong's Left Marshal, heard that Xiang Yu was angry and wanted to attack Pei Gong. He sent someone to tell Xiang Yu, "Pei Gong wants to become king of Guanzhong, make Zi Ying his chancellor, and keep all the precious treasures."

sentences.zh: 欲以求封。

translations.literal: He wanted to seek enfeoffment through this.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to seek enfeoffment through this.

sentences.zh: 亞父范增說羽曰：「沛公居山東時，貪財好色，今聞其入關，珍物無所取，婦女無所幸，此其志不小。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Fan Zeng advised Xiang Yu: "When Pei Gong was in Shandong, he was greedy for wealth and fond of women. Now we hear that upon entering the passes, he has taken none of the precious objects and favored none of the women. His ambitions are not small.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng, the Second Father, advised Xiang Yu: "When Pei Gong was east of the mountains, he was greedy for wealth and fond of women. Now we hear that after entering the passes, he has taken no precious objects and favored no women. His ambitions are not small.

sentences.zh: 吾使人望其氣，皆為龍，成五色，此天子氣。

translations.literal: I sent people to observe his aura, and it was all dragon-shaped, forming five colors. This is the aura of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I sent people to observe his aura, and it was all dragon-shaped, forming five colors. This is the aura of a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 急擊之，勿失。」

translations.literal: Attack him urgently. Do not miss the opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Attack him urgently. Do not miss the opportunity."

sentences.zh: 於是饗士，旦日合戰。

translations.literal: So he feasted his troops and the next day engaged in battle.
translations.idiomatic: So he feasted his troops and the next day engaged in battle.

sentences.zh: 是時，羽兵四十萬，號百萬。

translations.literal: At this time, Xiang Yu's troops numbered 400,000, claiming 1,000,000.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Xiang Yu's troops numbered 400,000, claiming 1,000,000.

sentences.zh: 沛公兵十萬，號二十萬，力不敵。

translations.literal: Pei Gong's troops numbered 100,000, claiming 200,000. Their strength was no match.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong's troops numbered 100,000, claiming 200,000. Their strength was no match.

sentences.zh: 會羽季父左尹項伯素善張良，夜馳見張良，具告其實，欲與俱去，毋特俱死。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu's uncle Xiang Bo had long been on good terms with Zhang Liang. He galloped at night to see Zhang Liang and told him everything in detail. He wanted to leave with him and not die together.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu's uncle, Left Yin Xiang Bo, had long been on good terms with Zhang Liang. He galloped at night to see Zhang Liang, told him everything in detail, and wanted Zhang Liang to leave with him rather than perish together for nothing.

sentences.zh: 良曰：「臣為韓王送沛公，不可不告，亡去不義。」

translations.literal: Liang said: "I was sent by the King of Han to escort Pei Gong. I cannot fail to inform him. To flee would be unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "The King of Han sent me to escort Pei Gong. I cannot fail to inform him; to flee would be unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 乃與項伯俱見沛公。

translations.literal: So he went with Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong.
translations.idiomatic: So he went with Xiang Bo to see Pei Gong.

sentences.zh: 沛公與伯約為婚姻，曰：「吾入關，秋豪無所敢取，籍吏民，封府庫，待將軍。

translations.literal: Pei Gong made a marriage alliance with Xiang Bo and said: "When I entered the passes, I dared not take even the smallest thing. I registered the officials and people, sealed the treasuries, and waited for the general.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gong formed a marriage alliance with Xiang Bo and said: "When I entered the passes, I dared not take even the smallest thing. I registered the officials and people, sealed the storehouses and treasuries, and waited for the general.

sentences.zh: 所以守關者，備他盜也。

translations.literal: The reason I guarded the passes was to prepare against other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I guarded the passes was to prepare against other bandits.

sentences.zh: 日夜望將軍到，豈敢反邪！

translations.literal: Day and night I hoped for the general's arrival. How could I dare rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I hoped for the general's arrival. How could I dare rebel!

sentences.zh: 願伯明言不敢背德。」

translations.literal: I hope Xiang Bo will make this clear that I dare not betray righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Xiang Bo will make this clear that I dare not betray righteousness."

sentences.zh: 項伯許諾，即夜復去。

translations.literal: Xiang Bo agreed and that night left again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bo agreed and that night left again.

sentences.zh: 戒沛公曰：「旦日不可不早自來謝。」

translations.literal: He warned Pei Gong: "Tomorrow morning you must not fail to come early and apologize."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bo warned Pei Gong: "Tomorrow you must come early to apologize."

sentences.zh: 項伯還，具以沛公言告羽，因曰：「沛公不先破關中兵，公巨能入乎？

translations.literal: Xiang Bo returned and told Xiang Yu everything Pei Gong had said. He added: "If Pei Gong had not first broken the Guanzhong troops, could you have entered?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bo returned and told Xiang Yu everything Pei Gong had said, then added, "If Pei Gong had not first defeated the Guanzhong troops, could you have entered?

sentences.zh: 且人有大功，擊之不祥，不如因善之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when someone has great merit, to attack him is inauspicious. It would be better to take advantage of and reward him."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when someone has great merit, to attack him is inauspicious. It would be better to take advantage of and reward him."

sentences.zh: 羽許諾。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 沛公旦日從百餘騎見羽鴻門，謝曰：「臣與將軍戮力攻秦，將軍戰河北，臣戰河南，不自意先入關，能破秦，與將軍復相見。

translations.literal: The next morning Pei Gong came with over a hundred cavalry to see Xiang Yu at Hongmen. He apologized: "I and the general joined forces to attack Qin. The general fought north of the Yellow River, I fought south of the Yellow River. I did not expect to enter the passes first and break Qin, then meet the general again.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, Pei Gong came with more than a hundred riders to see Xiang Yu at Hongmen and apologized: "I joined forces with the general to attack Qin. The general fought north of the Yellow River, and I fought south of it. I did not expect to enter the passes first, defeat Qin, and then meet the general again.

sentences.zh: 今者有小人言，令將軍與臣有隙。」

translations.literal: Now some petty person has spoken, causing the general and me to have a rift."
translations.idiomatic: Now some petty person has spoken, causing the general and me to have a rift."

sentences.zh: 羽曰：「此沛公左司馬曹毋傷言之，不然，籍何以生此？」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu said: "This was spoken by Pei Gong's left marshal Cao Wushang. Otherwise, how could I have thought this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu said: "This was reported by Pei Gong's left marshal Cao Wushang. Otherwise, how could such suspicions have arisen?"

sentences.zh: 羽因留沛公飲。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu then kept Pei Gong to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu then kept Pei Gong to drink.

sentences.zh: 范增數目羽擊沛公，羽不應。

translations.literal: Fan Zeng repeatedly signaled Xiang Yu to attack Pei Gong, but Xiang Yu did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng repeatedly signaled Xiang Yu to attack Pei Gong, but Xiang Yu did not respond.

sentences.zh: 范增起，出謂項莊曰：「

translations.literal: Fan Zeng rose and went out to tell Xiang Zhuang, “
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng rose, went out, and told Xiang Zhuang, “

sentences.zh: 君王為人不忍，汝入以劍舞，因擊沛公，殺之。

translations.literal: The lord is a man without mercy. You enter and perform the sword dance, then take advantage to strike Pei Gong and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord is too softhearted. Go in and perform a sword dance, then strike Pei Gong and kill him.

sentences.zh: 不者，汝屬且為所虜。」

translations.literal: If not, you and your clan will soon be his captives."
translations.idiomatic: If not, you and your clan will soon be his captives."

sentences.zh: 莊入為壽。

translations.literal: Xiang Zhuang entered and made a toast.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhuang entered and made a toast.

sentences.zh: 壽畢，曰：「軍中無以為樂，請以劍舞。」

translations.literal: When the toast was finished, he said: "There is nothing to provide entertainment in the army. Please allow me to perform the sword dance."
translations.idiomatic: When the toast was finished, Xiang Zhuang said: "There is nothing in camp for amusement. Please let me perform a sword dance."

sentences.zh: 因拔劍舞。

translations.literal: So he drew his sword and began to dance.
translations.idiomatic: So he drew his sword and began to dance.

sentences.zh: 項伯亦起舞，常以身翼蔽沛公。

translations.literal: Xiang Bo also rose to dance, constantly using his body to shield Pei Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bo also rose to dance, constantly using his body to shield Pei Gong.
