sentences.zh: 樊噲聞事急，直入，怒甚。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai heard the situation was urgent and charged straight in, extremely angry.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai heard the situation was urgent and charged straight in, extremely angry.

sentences.zh: 羽壯之，賜以酒。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu admired his bravery and gave him wine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu admired his bravery and gave him wine.

sentences.zh: 噲因譙讓羽。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai took advantage to rebuke Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai took advantage to rebuke Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 有頃，沛公起如廁，招樊噲出，置車官屬，獨騎，與樊噲、靳彊、滕公、紀成步，從間道走軍，使張良留謝羽。

translations.literal: After a while, Pei Gong rose as if to use the toilet and beckoned Fan Kuai to come out. He placed his chariot officials and retainers, rode alone with Fan Kuai, Jin Qiang, Lord Teng, and Ji Cheng on foot, escaping the army by a side road, leaving Zhang Liang to stay and apologize to Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After a while, Pei Gong rose as if to use the privy and beckoned Fan Kuai out. Leaving his carriages and attendants behind, he rode off alone, while Fan Kuai, Jin Qiang, Lord Teng, and Ji Cheng went on foot. They fled the camp by a side road, and he had Zhang Liang remain to apologize to Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽問：「沛公安在？」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu asked: "Where is Pei Gong?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu asked: "Where is Pei Gong?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「聞將軍有意督過之，脫身去，間至軍，故使臣獻璧。」

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said: "He heard that the general intended to punish him for his faults. He slipped away and secretly returned to his army. Therefore he sent me to present this jade disk."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said, "He heard that the general intended to hold him accountable for his faults, so he slipped away and returned secretly to his army. That is why he sent me to present this jade disk."

sentences.zh: 羽受之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又獻玉斗范增。

translations.literal: He also presented a jade goblet to Fan Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented a jade goblet to Fan Zeng.

sentences.zh: 增怒，撞其斗，起曰：「吾屬今為沛公虜矣！」

translations.literal: Fan Zeng was angry and smashed his goblet. He rose and said: "We and our clans will soon be Pei Gong's captives!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng was angry and smashed his goblet. He rose and said: "We and our clans will soon be Pei Gong's captives!"

sentences.zh: 沛公歸數日，羽引兵西屠咸陽，殺秦降王子嬰，燒秦宮室，所過無不殘滅。

translations.literal: Pei Gong returned several days later. Xiang Yu led troops west to massacre Xianyang, killed the Qin surrender prince Zi Ying, burned the Qin palaces. Everywhere he passed, nothing was left undestroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after Pei Gong returned, Xiang Yu led his troops west, slaughtered Xianyang, killed Zi Ying, the surrendered prince of Qin, and burned the Qin palaces. Wherever he passed, everything was devastated.

sentences.zh: 秦民大失望。

translations.literal: The Qin people were greatly disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin people were greatly disappointed.

sentences.zh: 羽使人還報懷王，懷王曰：「如約。」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu sent someone to report back to King Huai. King Huai said: "As agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu sent someone to report back to King Huai. King Huai said: "As agreed."

sentences.zh: 羽怨懷王不肯令與沛公俱西入關，而北救趙，後天下約。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu resented that King Huai had not allowed him to enter the passes together with Pei Gong, but instead had him go north to rescue Zhao, coming after the agreement about the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu resented King Huai for refusing to let him enter the passes westward together with Pei Gong, instead sending him north to rescue Zhao, so that he came too late for the agreement over the realm.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「

translations.literal: So he said, “
translations.idiomatic: So he said, “

sentences.zh: 懷王者，吾家所立耳，非有功伐，何以得專主約！

translations.literal: King Huai was established by my family, he has no meritorious achievements. Why should he monopolize the agreements!
translations.idiomatic: King Huai was installed by my family; he has won no merit in the conquest—why should he alone dictate the agreements!

sentences.zh: 本定天下，諸將與籍也。」

translations.literal: Originally it was the generals and I who pacified the world."
translations.idiomatic: Originally it was the generals and I who pacified the world."

sentences.zh: 春正月，陽尊懷王為義帝，實不用其命。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring, Yang honored King Huai as Righteous Emperor, but in reality did not follow his commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Xiang Yu nominally honored King Huai as the Righteous Emperor, but in reality did not obey his commands.

sentences.zh: 二月，羽自立為西楚霸王，王梁、楚地九郡，都彭城。

translations.literal: In the second month, Xiang Yu established himself as Hegemon King of Western Chu, ruling the lands of Liang and Chu, nine commanderies, with capital at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Xiang Yu established himself as Hegemon-King of Western Chu, ruling the nine commanderies of Liang and Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 背約，更立沛公為漢王，王巴、蜀、漢中四十一縣，都南鄭。

translations.literal: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 三分關中，立秦三將：章邯為雍王，都廢丘；

translations.literal: He divided Guanzhong into three parts, establishing the three Qin generals: Zhang Han as King of Yong, capital at Feiqiu;
translations.idiomatic: He divided Guanzhong into three parts, establishing the three Qin generals: Zhang Han as King of Yong, capital at Feiqiu;

sentences.zh: 司馬欣為塞王，都櫟陽；

translations.literal: Sima Xin as King of Sai, capital at Queyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin as King of Sai, capital at Queyang;

sentences.zh: 董翳為翟王，都高奴。

translations.literal: Dong Yi as King of Di, capital at Gaonu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yi as King of Di, capital at Gaonu.

sentences.zh: 楚將瑕丘申陽為河南王，都洛陽。

translations.literal: Chu general Xiaqiu Shen Yang as King of Henan, capital at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu general Xiaqiu Shen Yang as King of Henan, capital at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 趙將司馬卬為殷王，都朝歌。

translations.literal: Zhao general Sima Ang as King of Yin, capital at Zhaoge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao general Sima Ang as King of Yin, capital at Zhaoge.

sentences.zh: 當陽君英布為九江王，都六。

translations.literal: Dangyang Lord Ying Bu as King of Jiujiang, capital at Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Dangyang Lord Ying Bu as King of Jiujiang, capital at Liu.

sentences.zh: 懷王柱國共敖為臨江王，都江陵。

translations.literal: King Huai's Pillar of State Gong Ao as King of Linjiang, capital at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai's Pillar of State Gong Ao as King of Linjiang, capital at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 番君吳芮為衡山王，都邾。

translations.literal: Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Hengshan, capital at Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jun Wu Rui as King of Hengshan, capital at Zhu.

sentences.zh: 故齊王建孫田安為濟北王。

translations.literal: The former King of Qi Jian's grandson Tian An as King of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: The former King of Qi Jian's grandson Tian An as King of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 徙魏王豹為西魏王，都平陽。

translations.literal: Moved King of Wei Bao to King of Western Wei, capital at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Moved King of Wei Bao to King of Western Wei, capital at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 徙燕王韓廣為遼東王。

translations.literal: Moved King of Yan Han Guang to King of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Moved King of Yan Han Guang to King of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 燕將臧荼為燕王，都薊。

translations.literal: Yan general Zang Tu as King of Yan, capital at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yan general Zang Tu as King of Yan, capital at Ji.

sentences.zh: 徙齊王田市為膠東王。

translations.literal: Moved King of Qi Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Moved King of Qi Tian Shi to King of Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 齊將田都為齊王，都臨菑。

translations.literal: Qi general Tian Du as King of Qi, capital at Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi general Tian Du as King of Qi, capital at Linzi.

sentences.zh: 徙趙王歇為代王。

translations.literal: Moved King of Zhao Xie to King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Moved King of Zhao Xie to King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 趙相張耳為常山王。

translations.literal: Zhao chancellor Zhang Er as King of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao chancellor Zhang Er as King of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 漢王怨羽之背約，欲攻之，丞相蕭何諫，乃止。

translations.literal: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，諸侯罷戲下，各就國。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, the feudal lords departed from Xixia and each went to their kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the feudal lords departed from Xixia and each went to their kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 羽使卒三萬人從漢王，楚子、諸侯人之慕從者數萬人，從杜南入蝕中。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu sent 30,000 troops to follow King Han, and Chu nobles and feudal lords who admired and followed him numbered several tens of thousands. They entered Shuzhong from Dushan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu sent thirty thousand soldiers to accompany the King of Han, and several tens of thousands of Chu nobles and men from the feudal lords admired him and followed as well. They entered Shuzhong from south of Du.

sentences.zh: 張良辭歸韓，漢王送至褒中，因說漢王燒絕棧道，以備諸侯盜兵，亦視項羽無東意。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang took leave to return to Han. King Han escorted him to Baozhong, where Zhang Liang advised King Han to burn and destroy the plank roads to guard against bandit troops of the feudal lords, and also to show Xiang Yu that he had no intention of going east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang took leave to return to Han. The King of Han escorted him as far as Baozhong, and there Zhang Liang advised him to burn and sever the plank roads, both to guard against raiding troops from the feudal lords and to show Xiang Yu that he had no intention of going east.

sentences.zh: 漢王既至南鄭，諸將及士卒皆歌謳思東歸，多道亡還者。

translations.literal: King Han having arrived at Nanzheng, the generals and soldiers all sang ballads longing to return east, and many deserted and went back by the roads.
translations.idiomatic: After the King of Han reached Nanzheng, the generals and soldiers all sang songs longing to return east, and many deserted along the roads.

sentences.zh: 韓信為治粟都尉，亦亡去，蕭何追還之，因薦於漢王，曰：「

translations.literal: Han Xin was grain supply commander, but he also deserted. Xiao He pursued and brought him back, then recommended him to King Han, saying: "
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin was Commandant for Grain Supply, but he too deserted. Xiao He pursued him, brought him back, and then recommended him to the King of Han, saying: "

sentences.zh: 必欲爭天下，非信無可與計事者。」

translations.literal: If you truly wish to contend for the world, there is no one but Xin with whom you can plan affairs."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to contend for the world, there is no one but Xin with whom you can plan affairs."

sentences.zh: 於是漢王齊戒設壇場，拜信為大將軍，問以計策。

translations.literal: So King Han purified himself and set up an altar platform, appointing Xin as grand general and asking him for strategies.
translations.idiomatic: So King Han purified himself and set up an altar platform, appointing Xin as grand general and asking him for strategies.

sentences.zh: 信對曰：「項羽背約而王君王於南鄭，是遷也。

translations.literal: Xin replied: "Xiang Yu broke the agreement and enfeoffed you as king in Nanzheng. This was banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xin replied: "Xiang Yu broke the agreement and enfeoffed you as king in Nanzheng. This was banishment.

sentences.zh: 吏卒皆山東之人，日夜企而望歸，及其鋒而用之，可以有大功。

translations.literal: The officials and soldiers are all men from east of the mountains. Day and night they crane their necks longing to return home. If you take advantage of their keen edge and use them now, you can achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers are all men from east of the mountains. Day and night they stand on tiptoe longing to return home. If you use them now while their edge is sharp, you can achieve great merit.

sentences.zh: 天下已定，民皆自寧，不可復用。

translations.literal: When the world is pacified, the people will all be at peace. They cannot be used again.
translations.idiomatic: When the world is pacified, the people will all be at peace. They cannot be used again.

sentences.zh: 不如決策東向。」

translations.literal: It would be better to decide now and advance east."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to decide now and advance east."

sentences.zh: 因陳羽可圖三秦易并之計。

translations.literal: He then laid out the plan for how Xiang Yu could be plotted against and the three Qins easily united.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out his plan for seizing the three Qin states while Xiang Yu was occupied.

sentences.zh: 漢王大說，遂聽信策，部署諸將。

translations.literal: King Han was greatly pleased and followed Xin's strategy, deploying the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: King Han was greatly pleased and followed Xin's strategy, deploying the various generals.

sentences.zh: 留蕭何收巴蜀租，給軍食。

translations.literal: He left Xiao He to collect taxes from Ba and Shu to supply the army's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He left Xiao He to collect taxes from Ba and Shu to supply the army's provisions.

sentences.zh: 五月，漢王引兵從故道出襲雍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.

sentences.zh: 雍王邯迎擊漢陳倉，雍兵敗，還走；

translations.literal: King Yong Zhang Han met and attacked the Han army at Chencang. The Yong troops were defeated and fled back;
translations.idiomatic: King Yong Zhang Han met and attacked the Han army at Chencang. The Yong troops were defeated and fled back;

sentences.zh: 戰好畤，又大敗，走廢丘。

translations.literal: they fought at Haozhi and suffered another great defeat, fleeing to Feiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: they fought at Haozhi and suffered another great defeat, fleeing to Feiqiu.

sentences.zh: 漢王遂定雍地。

translations.literal: King Han then pacified Yong territory.
translations.idiomatic: King Han then pacified Yong territory.

sentences.zh: 東如咸陽，引兵圍雍王廢丘，而遣諸將略地。

translations.literal: He went east to Xianyang, led troops to surround King Yong at Feiqiu, and sent various generals to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: He went east to Xianyang, led troops to surround King Yong at Feiqiu, and sent various generals to seize territory.

sentences.zh: 田榮聞羽徙齊王市於膠東而立田都為齊王，大怒，以齊兵迎擊田都。

translations.literal: Tian Rong heard that Xiang Yu had moved King Qi Tian Shi to Jiaodong and established Tian Du as King of Qi. He was greatly angered and led Qi troops to attack Tian Du.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Rong heard that Xiang Yu had moved Tian Shi, King of Qi, to Jiaodong and installed Tian Du as King of Qi, he was furious and led the Qi troops to attack Tian Du.

sentences.zh: 都走降楚。

translations.literal: Tian Du fled and surrendered to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Du fled and surrendered to Chu.

sentences.zh: 六月，田榮殺田市，自立為齊王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Tian Rong killed Tian Shi and established himself as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Tian Rong killed Tian Shi and established himself as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 時彭城在鉅野，眾萬餘人，無所屬。

translations.literal: At this time Peng Yue was at Juye with over 10,000 followers, belonging to no one.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Peng Yue was at Juye with over 10,000 followers, belonging to no one.

sentences.zh: 榮與越將軍印，因令反梁地。

translations.literal: Tian Rong gave Peng Yue a general's seal and ordered him to rebel in Liang territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong gave Peng Yue a general's seal and ordered him to rebel in Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 越擊殺濟北王安，榮遂并三齊之地。

translations.literal: Yue attacked and killed King Jibei Tian An. Tian Rong then united the three Qi territories.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yue attacked and killed King of Jibei Tian An. Tian Rong then united the three Qi territories.

sentences.zh: 燕王韓廣亦不肯徙遼東。

translations.literal: King Yan Han Guang also refused to move to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: King Yan Han Guang also refused to move to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，臧荼殺韓廣，并其地。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Zang Tu killed Han Guang and took his territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, Zang Tu killed Han Guang and took his territory.

sentences.zh: 塞王欣、翟王翳皆降漢。

translations.literal: King Sai Xin and King Di Yi both surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: King Sai Xin and King Di Yi both surrendered to Han.

sentences.zh: 初，項梁立韓後公子成為韓王，張良為韓司徒。

translations.literal: Initially, Xiang Liang established the Han royal descendant Cheng as King of Han, with Zhang Liang as Han tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Xiang Liang established the Han royal descendant Cheng as King of Han, with Zhang Liang as Han tutor.

sentences.zh: 羽以良從漢王，韓王成又無功，故不遣就國，與俱至彭城，殺之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu, because Liang followed King Han, and King Han Cheng had no merit, did not send him to his kingdom but brought him to Pengcheng and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Liang had accompanied the King of Han (Liu Bang), and King Cheng of Han had achieved nothing, Xiang Yu would not let Cheng go to his kingdom; he brought Cheng to Pengcheng and killed him.

sentences.zh: 及聞漢王并關中，而齊、梁畔之，羽大怒，乃以故吳令鄭昌為韓王，距漢。

translations.literal: When he heard that King Han had united Guanzhong and Qi and Liang had rebelled, Xiang Yu was greatly angered. He established the former Wu magistrate Zheng Chang as King of Han to oppose Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu heard that the King of Han had taken all of Guanzhong and that Qi and Liang had rebelled against him, he was furious. He made Zheng Chang, the former magistrate of Wu, King of Han to block Han.

sentences.zh: 令蕭公角擊彭越，越敗角兵。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiao Gong Jiao to attack Peng Yue. Yue defeated Jiao's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xiao Gong Jiao to attack Peng Yue. Yue defeated Jiao's troops.

sentences.zh: 時張良徇韓地，遺羽書曰：「漢欲得關中，如約即止，不敢復東。」

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Liang was campaigning in Han territory. He sent Xiang Yu a letter: "Han wishes to obtain Guanzhong. If the agreement is honored, we will stop and dare not advance east again."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhang Liang was campaigning through Han territory. He sent Xiang Yu a letter: "Han only wishes to obtain Guanzhong. If the agreement is honored, we will stop and will not dare advance east again."

sentences.zh: 羽以故無西意，而北擊齊。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu therefore had no intention of going west, but instead attacked Qi to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu therefore had no intention of going west, but instead attacked Qi to the north.

sentences.zh: 九月，漢王遣將軍薛歐、王吸出武關，因王陵兵，從南陽迎太公、呂后於沛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Han sent generals Xue Ou and Wang Xi out of Wuguan, relying on Wang Ling's troops, going from Nanyang to welcome the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü from Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the King of Han sent Generals Xue Ou and Wang Xi out through Wuguan to join Wang Ling's troops and proceed from Nanyang to Pei to escort the Venerable Sire and Empress Lü.

sentences.zh: 羽聞之，發兵距之陽夏，不得前。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu heard of this and sent troops to block them at Yangxia, preventing them from advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu heard of this and sent troops to block them at Yangxia, preventing them from advancing.

sentences.zh: 二年冬十月，項羽使九江王布殺義帝於郴。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the second year, Xiang Yu ordered King Jiujiang Ying Bu to kill Righteous Emperor Huai at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the second year, Xiang Yu ordered King Jiujiang Ying Bu to kill Righteous Emperor Huai at Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳餘亦怨羽獨不王己，從田榮藉助兵，以擊常山王張耳。

translations.literal: Chen Yu also resented that Xiang Yu alone did not enfeoff him as king. He borrowed troops from Tian Rong and attacked King Changshan Zhang Er.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu also resented that Xiang Yu had not made him a king. He borrowed troops from Tian Rong and attacked Zhang Er, King of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 耳敗走降漢，漢王厚遇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Er was defeated, fled, and surrendered to Han. King Han treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er was defeated, fled, and surrendered to Han. King Han treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 陳餘迎代王歇還趙，歇立餘為代王。

translations.literal: Chen Yu welcomed King Dai Xie back to Zhao. Xie established Yu as King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu welcomed King Dai Xie back to Zhao. Xie established Yu as King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 張良自韓間行歸漢，漢王以為成信侯。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang secretly made his way back to Han from Korea. King Han enfeoffed him as Lord Chengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang stole his way back from Han to join the King of Han. The King of Han made him Lord Chengxin.

sentences.zh: 漢王如陝，鎮撫關外父老。

translations.literal: King Han went to Shan and pacified the elders outside the passes.
translations.idiomatic: King Han went to Shan and pacified the elders outside the passes.

sentences.zh: 河南王申陽降，置河南郡。

translations.literal: King Henan Shen Yang surrendered. Henan commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: King Henan Shen Yang surrendered. Henan commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 使韓太尉韓信擊韓，韓王鄭昌降。

translations.literal: He sent Han marshal Han Xin to attack Han. King Han Zheng Chang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han marshal Han Xin to attack Han. King Han Zheng Chang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，立韓太尉信為韓王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he established Han marshal Xin as King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, he established Han marshal Xin as King of Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王還歸，都櫟陽，使諸將略地，拔隴西。

translations.literal: King Han returned and established his capital at Queyang, sending various generals to seize territory and capture Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: King Han returned and established his capital at Queyang, sending various generals to seize territory and capture Longxi.

sentences.zh: 以萬人若一郡降者，封萬戶。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered with ten thousand men or an entire commandery were enfeoffed with ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrendered with ten thousand men or an entire commandery were enfeoffed with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 繕治河上塞。

translations.literal: He repaired the fortifications along the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the fortifications along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 故秦苑囿園池，令民得田之。

translations.literal: The former Qin parks, gardens, and ponds were opened so the people could farm them.
translations.idiomatic: The former Qin parks, gardens, and ponds were opened so the people could farm them.

sentences.zh: 春正月，羽擊田榮城陽，榮敗走平原，平原民殺之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Xiang Yu attacked Tian Rong at Chengyang. Rong was defeated and fled to Pingyuan, where the people of Pingyuan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Xiang Yu attacked Tian Rong at Chengyang. Rong was defeated and fled to Pingyuan, where the people killed him.

sentences.zh: 齊皆降楚，楚焚其城郭，齊人復畔之。

translations.literal: All of Qi surrendered to Chu. Chu burned their cities and walls, and the people of Qi rebelled against it again.
translations.idiomatic: All of Qi surrendered to Chu. Chu burned their cities and walls, and the people of Qi rebelled against it again.

sentences.zh: 諸將拔北地，虜雍王弟章平。

translations.literal: The generals took Beidi and captured Zhang Ping, the younger brother of the King of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The generals took Beidi and captured Zhang Ping, the younger brother of the King of Yong.

sentences.zh: 赦罪人。

translations.literal: Criminals were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，令民除秦社稷，立漢社稷。

translations.literal: On guiwei in the second month, the people were ordered to remove the Qin altars of soil and grain and establish the Han altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the second month, the people were ordered to remove the Qin altars of soil and grain and establish those of Han.

sentences.zh: 施恩德，賜民爵。

translations.literal: Grace and favor were bestowed, and ranks of nobility were granted to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Grace and favor were bestowed, and ranks of nobility were granted to the people.

sentences.zh: 蜀漢民給軍事勞苦，復勿租稅二歲。

translations.literal: The people of Shu and Han who had supplied the army and labored hard were exempted from rent and taxes for two years.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu and Han who had supplied the army and labored hard were exempted from rent and taxes for two years.

sentences.zh: 關中卒從軍者，復家一歲。

translations.literal: For soldiers from Guanzhong who had followed the army, their households were exempted for one year.
translations.idiomatic: For soldiers from Guanzhong who had followed the army, their households were exempted for one year.

sentences.zh: 舉民年五十以上，有脩行，能帥眾為善，置以為三老，鄉一人。

translations.literal: Among the people aged fifty and above, those of cultivated conduct who could lead others in doing good were selected and appointed as Three Elders, one for each township.
translations.idiomatic: Among people aged fifty and above, those of cultivated conduct who could lead others toward goodness were selected and appointed as Three Elders, one for each township.

sentences.zh: 擇鄉三老一人為縣三老，與縣令丞尉以事相教，復勿繇戍。

translations.literal: One township Three Elder was chosen to serve as the county Three Elder; together with the county magistrate, assistant, and commandant, he instructed the people in affairs, and he was exempted from corvee and garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: One township Three Elder was selected to serve as the county Three Elder. Together with the county magistrate, assistant, and commandant, he instructed the people in local affairs, and he was exempted from corvee and garrison service.

sentences.zh: 以十月賜酒肉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, wine and meat were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, wine and meat were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 三月，漢王自臨晉渡河，魏王豹降，將兵從。

translations.literal: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.

sentences.zh: 下河內，虜殷王卬，置河內郡。

translations.literal: He took Henan and captured King Yin Ang, establishing Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced Henei, captured King Yin Ang, and established Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 至脩武，陳平亡楚來降。

translations.literal: He reached Xiuwu. Chen Ping deserted Chu and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Xiuwu. Chen Ping deserted Chu and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 漢王與語，說之，使參乘，監諸將。

translations.literal: King Han spoke with him and was pleased. He had him ride in the chariot and oversee the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: King Han spoke with him and was pleased. He had him ride in the chariot and oversee the various generals.

sentences.zh: 南渡平陰津，至洛陽，新城三老董公遮說漢王曰：「臣聞『順德者昌，逆德者亡』，『兵出無名，事故不成』。

translations.literal: He crossed south at Pingyin ford and reached Luoyang. The elder of Xincheng, Dong Gong, blocked and advised King Han: "I have heard that 'those who follow virtue prosper, those who oppose virtue perish,' and 'when troops are sent out without just cause, affairs will not succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: He crossed south at Pingyin Ford and reached Luoyang. Dong Gong, the elder of Xincheng, stopped the King of Han and advised him: "I have heard, 'Those who follow virtue prosper; those who oppose virtue perish,' and, 'When troops are sent out without a proper name, the enterprise will not succeed.'

sentences.zh: 故曰：『明其為賊，敵乃可服。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'Make clear that he is the traitor, and the enemy can then be subdued.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: 'Make clear that he is the traitor, and the enemy can then be subdued.'

sentences.zh: 項羽為無道，放殺其主，天下之賊也。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu acts without righteousness, having deposed and killed his lord. He is the traitor of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu acts without righteousness, having deposed and killed his lord. He is the traitor of the world.

sentences.zh: 夫仁不以勇，義不以力，三軍之眾為之素服，以告之諸侯，為此東伐，四海之內莫不仰德。

translations.literal: Benevolence does not rely on bravery, righteousness does not rely on strength. The multitudes of the three armies will sincerely submit to you. Proclaim this to the feudal lords and then advance east. All within the four seas will look up to your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence does not rely on bravery, righteousness does not rely on force. Have the armies dress in mourning and proclaim this to the feudal lords, then march east—all within the four seas will look up to your virtue.

sentences.zh: 此三王之舉也。」

translations.literal: This is the undertaking of the Three Kings."
translations.idiomatic: This is the course of action of the Three Kings."

sentences.zh: 漢王曰：「善，非夫子無所聞。」

translations.literal: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."
translations.idiomatic: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."

sentences.zh: 於是漢王為義帝發喪，袒而大哭，哀臨三日。

translations.literal: So King Han held mourning rites for the Righteous Emperor, bared his shoulder and wept loudly, conducting the mourning rites for three days.
translations.idiomatic: So King Han held mourning rites for the Righteous Emperor, bared his shoulder and wept loudly, conducting the mourning rites for three days.

sentences.zh: 發使告諸侯曰：「

translations.literal: He sent envoys to proclaim to the feudal lords, “
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to proclaim to the lords, “

sentences.zh: 天下共立義帝，北面事之。

translations.literal: The realm jointly enthroned the Righteous Emperor and served him facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The realm jointly enthroned the Righteous Emperor and served him facing north.

sentences.zh: 今項羽放殺義帝江南，大逆無道。

translations.literal: Now Xiang Yu has deposed and killed the Righteous Emperor in Jiangnan. This is great rebellion without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiang Yu has deposed and killed the Righteous Emperor in Jiangnan. This is great rebellion without righteousness.

sentences.zh: 寡人親為發喪，兵皆縞素。

translations.literal: I personally conduct the mourning rites. All troops wear white mourning clothes.
translations.idiomatic: I personally conduct the mourning rites. All troops wear white mourning clothes.

sentences.zh: 悉發關中兵，收三河士，南浮江漢以下，願從諸侯王擊楚之殺義帝者。」

translations.literal: Mobilize all Guanzhong troops, gather the warriors of the three river regions, float south on the Jiang and Han rivers and below, and wish to follow the feudal lords to attack those who killed the Righteous Emperor in Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Mobilize all Guanzhong troops, gather the warriors of the three rivers, float south along the Jiang and Han, and wish to follow the feudal lords in attacking Chu for killing the Righteous Emperor."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，田榮弟橫收得數萬人，立榮子廣為齊王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Tian Rong's younger brother Heng gathered several tens of thousands of men and established Tian Rong's son Guang as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Tian Rong's younger brother Heng gathered several tens of thousands of men and established Rong's son Guang as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 羽雖聞漢東，既擊齊，欲遂破之而後擊漢，漢王以故得劫五諸侯兵，東伐楚。

translations.literal: Although Xiang Yu heard that Han was advancing east, since he was attacking Qi, he wished to completely defeat Qi first and then attack Han. King Han therefore was able to coerce the five feudal lords' troops and advance east to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiang Yu heard that Han was advancing east, he was already attacking Qi and wanted to crush it completely before turning against Han. The King of Han was therefore able to take command of the five feudal lords' troops and advance east to attack Chu.

sentences.zh: 到外黃，彭越將三萬人歸漢。

translations.literal: He reached Waihuang. Peng Yue led 30,000 men and surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Waihuang. Peng Yue led 30,000 men and surrendered to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王拜越為魏相國，令定梁地。

translations.literal: King Han appointed Yue as prime minister of Wei and ordered him to pacify Liang territory.
translations.idiomatic: King Han appointed Yue as prime minister of Wei and ordered him to pacify Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 漢王遂入彭城，收羽美人貨賂，置酒高會。

translations.literal: King Han then entered Pengcheng, took Xiang Yu's beautiful women and treasures, and held a great banquet.
translations.idiomatic: King Han then entered Pengcheng, took Xiang Yu's beautiful women and treasures, and held a great banquet.

sentences.zh: 羽聞之，令其將擊齊，而自以精兵三萬人從魯出胡陵，至蕭，晨擊漢軍，大戰彭城靈壁東睢水上，大破漢軍，多殺士卒，睢水為之不流。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu heard of this and ordered his generals to attack Qi, while he himself led 30,000 elite troops from Lu through Huling to Xiao. At dawn he attacked the Han army, fighting a great battle east of Pengcheng at Lingbi on the Sui River. He greatly defeated the Han army, killing many soldiers and officers. The Sui River stopped flowing because of the bodies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu heard of this, he ordered his generals to attack Qi, while he himself led thirty thousand picked troops from Lu through Huling to Xiao. At dawn he attacked the Han army and fought a great battle east of Pengcheng, at Lingbi on the Sui River. He inflicted a crushing defeat on Han, killing many officers and soldiers, so that the Sui River stopped flowing.

sentences.zh: 圍漢王三匝。

translations.literal: He surrounded King Han three times.
translations.idiomatic: He surrounded King Han three times.

sentences.zh: 大風從西北起，折木發屋，揚砂石，晝晦，楚軍大亂，而漢王得與數十騎遁去。

translations.literal: A great wind arose from the northwest, breaking trees and tearing off roofs, whipping up sand and stones, darkening the day. The Chu army was greatly thrown into confusion, and King Han was able to escape with several dozen cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind rose from the northwest, snapping trees, tearing roofs from houses, and whipping up sand and stones until daylight turned dark. The Chu army was thrown into chaos, and the King of Han escaped with several dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 過沛，使人求室家，室家亦已亡，不相得。

translations.literal: Passing through Pei, he sent people to seek his family. His family had also fled and they could not find each other.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Pei, he sent people to seek his family. His family had also fled and they could not find each other.

sentences.zh: 漢王道逢孝惠、魯元，載行。

translations.literal: King Han met Xiaohui and Lu Yuan on the road and had them ride in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: King Han met Xiaohui and Lu Yuan on the road and had them ride in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 楚騎追漢王，漢王急，推墮二子。

translations.literal: Chu cavalry pursued King Han. King Han was desperate and pushed the two children off the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chu cavalry pursued King Han. King Han was desperate and pushed the two children off the carriage.

sentences.zh: 滕公下收載，遂得脫。

translations.literal: Lord Teng dismounted to pick them up and put them in the carriage, and thus they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Teng dismounted to pick them up and put them in the carriage, and thus they escaped.

sentences.zh: 審食其從太公、呂后間行，反遇楚軍，羽常置軍中以為質。

translations.literal: Shen Yiji secretly escorted the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü, but encountered Chu troops. Xiang Yu constantly kept them in the army as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiji escorted the Venerable Sire and Empress Lü along hidden paths, but they encountered Chu troops. Xiang Yu kept them with the army as hostages.

sentences.zh: 諸侯見漢敗，皆亡去。

translations.literal: The feudal lords saw that Han was defeated and all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords saw that Han was defeated and all fled.

sentences.zh: 塞王欣、翟王翳降楚，殷王卬死。

translations.literal: King Sai Xin and King Di Yi surrendered to Chu. King Yin Ang died.
translations.idiomatic: King Sai Xin and King Di Yi surrendered to Chu. King Yin Ang died.

sentences.zh: 呂后兄周呂侯將兵居下邑，漢王往從之。

translations.literal: Empress Lü's elder brother Zhou Lühou led troops stationed at Xiayi. King Han went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü's elder brother Zhou Lühou led troops stationed at Xiayi. King Han went to join him.

sentences.zh: 稍收士卒，軍碭。

translations.literal: He gradually gathered soldiers and officers, encamping at Dang.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually gathered soldiers and officers, encamping at Dang.

sentences.zh: 漢王西過梁地，至虞，謂謁者隨何曰：「公能說九江王布使舉兵畔楚，項王必留擊之。

translations.literal: King Han passed west through Liang territory and reached Yu. He said to the usher Sui He: "You can persuade King Jiujiang Ying Bu to raise troops and rebel against Chu. Xiang Yu will certainly stay to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han passed west through Liang territory and reached Yu. He said to the usher Sui He: "Can you persuade Ying Bu, King of Jiujiang, to raise troops and rebel against Chu? Xiang Yu will certainly stay behind to attack him.

sentences.zh: 得留數月，吾取天下必矣。」

translations.literal: If we can hold him back for several months, I will certainly take the world."
translations.idiomatic: If we can hold him back for several months, I will certainly take the world."

sentences.zh: 隨何往說布，果使畔楚。

translations.literal: Sui He went to persuade Ying Bu, and indeed made him rebel against Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Sui He went to persuade Ying Bu, and indeed made him rebel against Chu.

sentences.zh: 五月，漢王屯滎陽，蕭何發關中老弱未傅者悉詣軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, King Han encamped at Xingyang. Xiao He conscripted all the old and weak in Guanzhong who had not yet been registered and sent them all to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the King of Han encamped at Xingyang. Xiao He called up all the old and weak men in Guanzhong who had not yet been registered for service and sent them to the army.

sentences.zh: 韓信亦收兵與漢王會，兵復大振。

translations.literal: Han Xin also gathered troops and joined King Han. The army was greatly strengthened again.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin also gathered troops and joined King Han. The army was greatly strengthened again.

sentences.zh: 與楚戰滎陽南京、索間，破之。

translations.literal: They fought Chu at Xingyang south of Nanjing and between the Suo River, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Chu between Jing and Suo, south of Xingyang, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 築甬道，屬河，以取敖倉粟。

translations.literal: They built a covered walkway connecting to the Yellow River to obtain grain from Aocang.
translations.idiomatic: They built a covered walkway connecting to the Yellow River to obtain grain from Aocang.

sentences.zh: 魏王豹謁歸視親疾。

translations.literal: King Wei Bao took leave to return and visit his ailing parent.
translations.idiomatic: King Wei Bao took leave to return and visit his ailing parent.

sentences.zh: 至則絕河津，反為楚。

translations.literal: Upon arriving, he cut off the river crossings and rebelled for Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arriving, he cut off the river crossings and rebelled for Chu.

sentences.zh: 六月，漢王還櫟陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, King Han returned to Queyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, King Han returned to Queyang.

sentences.zh: 壬午，立太子，赦罪人。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, he established the crown prince and pardoned criminals.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, he established the crown prince and pardoned criminals.

sentences.zh: 令諸侯子在關中者皆集櫟陽為衛。

translations.literal: He ordered all the feudal lords' sons in Guanzhong to assemble at Queyang as guards.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all the feudal lords' sons in Guanzhong to assemble at Queyang as guards.

sentences.zh: 引水灌廢丘，廢丘降，章邯自殺。

translations.literal: He diverted water to flood Feiqiu. Feiqiu surrendered. Zhang Han committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted water to flood Feiqiu. Feiqiu surrendered. Zhang Han committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 雍州定，八十餘縣，置河上、渭南、中地、隴西、上郡。

translations.literal: Yong province was pacified with over 80 counties. He established Heshang, Weinan, Zhongdi, Longxi, and Shangjun commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yong province was pacified with over 80 counties. He established Heshang, Weinan, Zhongdi, Longxi, and Shangjun commanderies.

sentences.zh: 令祠官祀天地四方上帝山川，以時祠之。

translations.literal: He ordered the ritual officials to sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, the Four Directions, Supreme Deities, mountains, and rivers, making sacrifices at the proper times.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ritual officials to sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, the Four Directions, Supreme Deities, mountains, and rivers, making sacrifices at the proper times.

sentences.zh: 興關中卒乘邊塞。

translations.literal: He raised Guanzhong troops to garrison the border fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Guanzhong troops to garrison the border fortifications.

sentences.zh: 關中大飢，米斛萬錢，人相食。

translations.literal: Guanzhong suffered great famine. Rice cost 10,000 cash per bushel. People ate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong suffered great famine. Rice cost 10,000 cash per bushel. People ate each other.

sentences.zh: 令民就食蜀漢。

translations.literal: He ordered the people to go to Shu and Han for food.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the people to go to Shu and Han for food.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，漢王如滎陽，謂酈食其曰：「緩頰往說魏王豹，能下之，以魏地萬戶封生。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, King Han went to Xingyang and said to Li Yiji: "Go slowly to persuade King Wei Bao. If you can make him submit, I will enfeoff you with 10,000 households from Wei territory."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, the King of Han went to Xingyang and said to Li Yiji: "Go and talk Wei Bao into submission with your eloquence. If you can bring him down, I will enfeoff you with ten thousand households from Wei territory."

sentences.zh: 食其往，豹不聽。

translations.literal: Li Yiji went, but Bao did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiji went, but Bao did not listen.

sentences.zh: 漢王以韓信為左丞相，與曹參、灌嬰俱擊魏。

translations.literal: King Han appointed Han Xin as left chancellor, and together with Cao Shen and Guan Ying attacked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: King Han appointed Han Xin as left chancellor, and together with Cao Shen and Guan Ying attacked Wei.

sentences.zh: 食其還，漢王問：「魏大將誰也？」

translations.literal: Li Yiji returned. King Han asked: "Who is Wei's chief general?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiji returned. King Han asked: "Who is Wei's chief general?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「柏直。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Bai Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Bai Zhi."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「是口尚乳臭，不能當韓信。

translations.literal: The king said: "His mouth still smells of milk. He cannot face Han Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The king said: "He's still wet behind the ears. He cannot stand up to Han Xin.

sentences.zh: 騎將誰也？」

translations.literal: Who is their cavalry general?"
translations.idiomatic: Who is their cavalry general?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「馮敬。」

translations.literal: He said: "Feng Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiji replied: "Feng Jing."

sentences.zh: 曰：「是秦將馮無擇子也，雖賢，不能當灌嬰。

translations.literal: He said: "He is the son of the Qin general Feng Wuzhe. Though capable, he cannot face Guan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The king said: "He is the son of the Qin general Feng Wuzhe. Though capable, he cannot stand up to Guan Ying.

sentences.zh: 步卒將誰也？」

translations.literal: Who is their infantry general?"
translations.idiomatic: Who is their infantry general?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「項它。」

translations.literal: He said: "Xiang Tuo."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Xiang Tuo."

sentences.zh: 曰：「是不能當曹參。

translations.literal: He said: "He cannot face Cao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The king said: "He cannot stand up to Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 吾無患矣。」

translations.literal: I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: I have no worries."

sentences.zh: 九月，信等虜豹，傳詣滎陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xin and others captured Bao and sent him to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xin and others captured Bao and sent him to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 定魏地，置河東、太原、上黨郡。

translations.literal: They pacified Wei territory and established Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: They pacified Wei territory and established Hedong, Taiyuan, and Shangdang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 信使人請兵三萬人，願以北舉燕趙，東擊齊，南絕楚糧道。

translations.literal: Xin sent someone to request 30,000 troops, wishing to advance north against Yan and Zhao, east against Qi, and south to cut off Chu's grain routes.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin sent someone to request thirty thousand troops, saying he wished to move north against Yan and Zhao, east against Qi, and south to cut off Chu's supply routes.

sentences.zh: 漢王與之。

translations.literal: King Han agreed.
translations.idiomatic: King Han agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年冬十月，韓信、張耳東下井陘擊趙，斬陳餘，獲趙王歇。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the third year, Han Xin and Zhang Er advanced east through Jingxing to attack Zhao, executed Chen Yu, and captured King Zhao Xie.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month of the third year, Han Xin and Zhang Er advanced east through Jingxing to attack Zhao, killed Chen Yu, and captured Xie, King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 置常山、代郡。

translations.literal: They established Changshan and Dai commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: They established Changshan and Dai commanderies.

sentences.zh: 甲戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸卯晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the day guimao last day of the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao last day of the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 隨何既說黥布，布起兵攻楚。

translations.literal: After Sui He persuaded Ying Bu, Bu raised troops to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui He persuaded Ying Bu, Bu raised troops to attack Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚使項聲、龍且攻布，布戰不勝。

translations.literal: Chu sent Xiang Sheng and Long Ju to attack Bu. Bu fought but was not victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Chu sent Xiang Sheng and Long Ju to attack Bu. Bu fought but was not victorious.

sentences.zh: 十二月，布與隨何間行歸漢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Bu and Sui He secretly made their way back to Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Bu and Sui He secretly made their way back to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王分之兵，與俱收兵至成皋。

translations.literal: King Han divided his troops with them and together gathered troops to reach Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: King Han divided his troops with them and together gathered troops to reach Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 項羽數侵奪漢甬道，漢軍乏食，與酈食其謀橈楚權。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu repeatedly invaded and seized Han's covered walkway. The Han army lacked food. He consulted with Li Yiji about weakening Chu's power.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu repeatedly invaded and seized Han's covered walkway. The Han army lacked food. He consulted with Li Yiji about weakening Chu's power.

sentences.zh: 食其欲立六國後以樹黨，漢王刻印，將遣食其立之。

translations.literal: Li Yiji wished to establish the descendants of the six kingdoms to create allies. King Han carved seals and was about to send Li Yiji to establish them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiji wanted to establish descendants of the six kingdoms in order to build a bloc of allies. The King of Han had seals carved and was about to send Li Yiji to install them.

sentences.zh: 以問張良，良發八難。

translations.literal: He asked Zhang Liang about it. Liang presented eight difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zhang Liang about it. Liang presented eight difficulties.

sentences.zh: 漢王輟飯吐哺，曰：「豎儒幾敗乃公事！」

translations.literal: King Han put down his food and spat it out, saying: "This pedantic scholar almost ruined your lord's affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han put down his food and spat it out, saying: "You pedant! You nearly ruined my whole plan!"

sentences.zh: 令趨銷印。

translations.literal: He ordered them to hurry and destroy the seals.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to hurry and destroy the seals.

sentences.zh: 又問陳平，乃從其計，與平黃金四萬斤，以間疏楚君臣。

translations.literal: He also asked Chen Ping, then followed his plan, giving Ping 40,000 jin of gold to sow dissension and alienate Chu's ruler and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Chen Ping, then followed his plan, giving Ping 40,000 jin of gold to sow dissension and alienate Chu's ruler and ministers.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，項羽圍漢滎陽，漢王請和，割滎陽以西者為漢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Xiang Yu surrounded Han at Xingyang. King Han requested peace, offering to divide Xingyang west as Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Xiang Yu surrounded Han at Xingyang. King Han requested peace, offering to divide Xingyang west as Han territory.

sentences.zh: 亞父勸項羽急攻滎陽，漢王患之。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Fan advised Xiang Yu to urgently attack Xingyang. King Han was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Prime Minister Fan advised Xiang Yu to urgently attack Xingyang. King Han was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 陳平反間既行，羽果疑亞父。

translations.literal: Chen Ping's reverse espionage having succeeded, Xiang Yu indeed suspected Prime Minister Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping's reverse espionage having succeeded, Xiang Yu indeed suspected Prime Minister Fan.

sentences.zh: 亞父大怒而去，發病死。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Fan was greatly angered and left. He fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Prime Minister Fan was greatly angered and left. He fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 五月，將軍紀信曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: In the fifth month, General Ji Xin said: "The situation is urgent!
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, General Ji Xin said: "The situation is urgent!

sentences.zh: 臣請誑楚，可以間出。」

translations.literal: I request to deceive Chu so we can break out."
translations.idiomatic: I request to deceive Chu so we can break out."

sentences.zh: 於是陳平夜出女子東門二千餘人，楚因四面擊之。

translations.literal: So Chen Ping at night sent out over 2,000 women through the east gate. Chu then attacked from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: So Chen Ping at night sent out over 2,000 women through the east gate. Chu then attacked from all four sides.

sentences.zh: 紀信乃乘王車，黃屋左纛，曰：「食盡，漢王降楚。」

translations.literal: Ji Xin then rode in the king's chariot with yellow canopy and left banner, saying: "Food is exhausted. King Han surrenders to Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xin then rode in the king's chariot with yellow canopy and left banner, saying: "Food is exhausted. King Han surrenders to Chu."

sentences.zh: 楚皆呼萬歲，之城東觀，以故漢王得與數十騎出西門遁。

translations.literal: All the Chu troops shouted ten thousand years. They went to the east wall to watch, so King Han was able to escape with several dozen cavalry through the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: All the Chu troops shouted, "Ten thousand years!" and went to the eastern side of the city to watch. Because of this, the King of Han escaped through the west gate with several dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 令御史大夫周苛、魏豹、樅公守滎陽。

translations.literal: He ordered Imperial Secretary Zhou Ke, Wei Bao, and Lord Song to defend Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Imperial Secretary Zhou Ke, Wei Bao, and Lord Song to defend Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 羽見紀信，問：「漢王安在？」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「已出去矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "He has already left."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xin said: "He has already left."

sentences.zh: 羽燒殺信。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu burned and killed Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu burned and killed Xin.

sentences.zh: 而周苛、樅公相謂曰：「反國之王，難與守城。」

translations.literal: Zhou Ke and Lord Song said to each other: "The king of a rebellious kingdom is difficult to defend the city with."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ke and Lord Song said to each other: "He is a rebel king—we cannot hold the city with him."

sentences.zh: 因殺魏豹。

translations.literal: So they killed Wei Bao.
translations.idiomatic: So they killed Wei Bao.

sentences.zh: 漢王出滎陽，至成皋。

translations.literal: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 自成皋入關，收兵欲復東。

translations.literal: From Chenggao he entered the passes, gathered troops, and wanted to advance east again.
translations.idiomatic: From Chenggao he entered the passes, gathered troops, and wanted to advance east again.

sentences.zh: 轅生說漢王曰：「漢與楚相距滎陽數歲，漢常困。

translations.literal: Guan Sheng advised King Han: "Han and Chu have confronted each other at Xingyang for several years. Han has often been in difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Sheng advised King Han: "Han and Chu have confronted each other at Xingyang for several years. Han has often been in difficulty.

sentences.zh: 願君王出武關，項王必引兵南走，王深壁，令滎陽成皋間且得休息。

translations.literal: I hope your majesty will go out through Wuguan. Xiang Yu will certainly lead troops south. Your majesty should fortify deeply and let the area between Xingyang and Chenggao get some rest.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to go out through Wuguan. Xiang Yu will certainly lead his troops south. Your Majesty should hold deep behind fortifications and let the area between Xingyang and Chenggao gain some respite.

sentences.zh: 使韓信等得輯河北趙地，連燕齊，君王乃復走滎陽。

translations.literal: Let Han Xin and others consolidate the lands north of the Yellow River in Zhao, connecting Yan and Qi. Your majesty can then return to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Let Han Xin and the others consolidate Zhao territory north of the Yellow River and link up with Yan and Qi. Your Majesty can then return to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 如此，則楚所備者多，力分。

translations.literal: In this way, Chu will have many places to defend, and their strength will be divided.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, Chu will have many places to defend, and their strength will be divided.

sentences.zh: 漢得休息，復與之戰，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Han will get rest, then fight them again. Defeating them will certainly be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Han will get rest, then fight them again. Defeating them will certainly be possible."

sentences.zh: 漢王從其計，出軍宛葉間，與黥布行收兵。

translations.literal: King Han followed his plan, led troops out between Wan and Ye, and together with Ying Bu went to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: King Han followed his plan, led troops out between Wan and Ye, and together with Ying Bu went to gather troops.

sentences.zh: 羽聞漢王在宛，果引兵南，漢王堅壁不與戰。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu heard that King Han was at Wan and indeed led troops south. King Han fortified deeply and did not fight him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu heard that King Han was at Wan and indeed led troops south. King Han fortified deeply and did not fight him.

sentences.zh: 是月，彭越渡睢，與項聲、薛公戰下邳，破殺薛公。

translations.literal: In this month, Peng Yue crossed the Sui River and fought Xiang Sheng and Xue Gong at Xiapi, defeating and killing Xue Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In this month, Peng Yue crossed the Sui River and fought Xiang Sheng and Xue Gong at Xiapi, defeating and killing Xue Gong.

sentences.zh: 羽使終公守成皋，而自東擊彭越。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu had Zhong Gong defend Chenggao while he himself went east to attack Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu had Zhong Gong defend Chenggao while he himself went east to attack Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 漢王引兵北，擊破終公，復軍成皋。

translations.literal: King Han led troops north, attacked and defeated Zhong Gong, and returned his army to Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: King Han led troops north, attacked and defeated Zhong Gong, and returned his army to Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 六月，羽已破走彭越，聞漢復軍成皋，乃引兵西拔滎陽城，生得周苛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Xiang Yu had already defeated and routed Peng Yue. He heard that Han had returned his army to Chenggao, so he led troops west and captured Xingyang city, taking Zhou Ke alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, after Xiang Yu had defeated and driven off Peng Yue, he heard that Han had again stationed troops at Chenggao. He therefore led his army west, took the city of Xingyang, and captured Zhou Ke alive.

sentences.zh: 羽謂苛：「為我將，以公為上將軍，封三萬戶。」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu said to Ke: "Be my general. I will make you supreme general and enfeoff you with 30,000 households."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu said to Ke: "Be my general. I will make you supreme general and enfeoff you with 30,000 households."

sentences.zh: 周苛罵曰：「若不趨降漢，今為虜矣！

translations.literal: Zhou Ke cursed: "If you do not quickly surrender to Han, you will now become a captive!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ke cursed: "If you do not quickly surrender to Han, you will now become a captive!

sentences.zh: 若非漢王敵也。」

translations.literal: You are no match for King Han."
translations.idiomatic: You are no match for King Han."

sentences.zh: 羽亨周苛，并殺樅公，而虜韓王信，遂圍成皋。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu boiled Zhou Ke and also killed Lord Song. He captured King Han Xin and then surrounded Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu boiled Zhou Ke and also killed Lord Song. He captured King Han Xin and then surrounded Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 漢王跳，獨與滕公共車出成皋玉門，北渡河，宿小脩武。

translations.literal: King Han leapt away, alone with Lord Teng sharing a chariot out of Chenggao's Jade Gate. They crossed north over the Yellow River and stayed at Xiao Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han escaped suddenly, sharing a chariot only with Lord Teng as he left Chenggao by the Jade Gate. They crossed the Yellow River northward and spent the night at Xiao Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 自稱使者，晨馳入張耳、韓信壁，而奪之軍。

translations.literal: He called himself an envoy and at dawn galloped into Zhang Er and Han Xin's encampment, seizing command of their army.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself an envoy and at dawn galloped into Zhang Er and Han Xin's encampment, seizing command of their army.

sentences.zh: 乃使張耳北收兵趙地。

translations.literal: He then had Zhang Er go north to gather troops in Zhao territory.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zhang Er go north to gather troops in Zhao territory.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，有星孛于大角。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, a comet appeared at Dajiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, a comet appeared at Dajiao.

sentences.zh: 漢王得韓信軍，復大振。

translations.literal: King Han got Han Xin's army and was greatly strengthened again.
translations.idiomatic: King Han got Han Xin's army and was greatly strengthened again.

sentences.zh: 八月，臨河南鄉，軍小脩武，欲復戰。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he faced Henan Xiang, encamped at Xiao Xiuwu, wanting to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, he faced Henan Xiang, encamped at Xiao Xiuwu, wanting to fight again.

sentences.zh: 郎中鄭忠說止漢王，高壘深塹勿戰。

translations.literal: Attendant Zheng Zhong advised King Han to stop, building high fortifications and deep moats without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zheng Zhong advised King Han to stop, building high fortifications and deep moats without fighting.

sentences.zh: 漢王聽其計，使盧綰、劉賈將卒二萬人，騎數百，渡白馬津入楚地，佐彭越燒楚積聚，復擊破楚軍燕郭西，攻下睢陽、外黃十七城。

translations.literal: King Han followed his plan, sending Lu Wan and Liu Jia with 20,000 troops and several hundred cavalry across Baima ford into Chu territory. They assisted Peng Yue in burning Chu's grain stores, then attacked and broke the Chu army west of Yan Guo, capturing Suiyang and Waihuang, 17 cities.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han followed his plan, sending Lu Wan and Liu Jia with twenty thousand soldiers and several hundred riders across Baima Ford into Chu territory. They assisted Peng Yue in burning Chu's stockpiles, then attacked and defeated the Chu army west of Yanguo, capturing seventeen cities, including Suiyang and Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 九月，羽謂海春侯大司馬曹咎曰：「謹守成皋。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xiang Yu said to Hai Chun Marquis Grand Marshal Cao Jiu: "Carefully guard Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xiang Yu said to Hai Chun Marquis Grand Marshal Cao Jiu: "Carefully guard Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 即漢王欲挑戰，慎勿與戰，勿令得東而已。

translations.literal: If King Han wants to provoke battle, be careful not to fight him. Just do not let him get east.
translations.idiomatic: If King Han wants to provoke battle, be careful not to fight him. Just do not let him get east.

sentences.zh: 我十五日必定梁地，復從將軍。」

translations.literal: Within 15 days I will certainly pacify Liang territory, then follow the general again."
translations.idiomatic: Within 15 days I will certainly pacify Liang territory, then follow the general again."

sentences.zh: 羽引兵東擊彭越。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu led troops east to attack Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu led troops east to attack Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 漢王使酈食其說齊王田廣，罷守兵與漢和。

translations.literal: King Han sent Li Yiji to persuade King Qi Tian Guang to dismiss his guarding troops and make peace with Han.
translations.idiomatic: King Han sent Li Yiji to persuade King Qi Tian Guang to dismiss his guarding troops and make peace with Han.

sentences.zh: 四年冬十月，韓信用蒯通計，襲破齊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the fourth year, Han Xin used Kuai Tong's plan and attacked, breaking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the fourth year, Han Xin used Kuai Tong's plan and attacked, breaking Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊王亨酈生，東走高密。

translations.literal: King Qi boiled Li Sheng and fled east to Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: King Qi had Li Yiji boiled alive and fled east to Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 項羽聞韓信破齊，且欲擊楚，使龍且救齊。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu heard that Han Xin had broken Qi and was about to attack Chu, so he sent Long Ju to rescue Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu heard that Han Xin had broken Qi and was about to attack Chu, so he sent Long Ju to rescue Qi.

sentences.zh: 漢果數挑成皋戰，楚軍不出，使人辱之數日，大司馬咎怒，渡兵汜水。

translations.literal: Han repeatedly provoked battle at Chenggao, but the Chu army did not come out. They sent people to insult them for several days. Grand Marshal Jiu was angry and crossed his troops over Sishui River.
translations.idiomatic: Han repeatedly challenged the Chu army at Chenggao, but the Chu forces would not come out. Han sent men to insult them for several days, until Grand Marshal Jiu became angry and led his troops across the Si River.

sentences.zh: 士卒半渡，漢擊之，大破楚軍，盡得楚國金玉貨賂。

translations.literal: The soldiers were half across when Han attacked them, greatly defeating the Chu army and obtaining all of Chu's gold, jade, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were half across when Han attacked them, greatly defeating the Chu army and obtaining all of Chu's gold, jade, and treasures.

sentences.zh: 大司馬咎、長史欣皆自剄汜水上。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Jiu and Chief Secretary Xin both committed suicide on the Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Jiu and Chief Secretary Xin both committed suicide on the Sishui.

sentences.zh: 漢王引兵渡河，復取成皋，軍廣武，就敖倉食。

translations.literal: King Han led troops across the river, recaptured Chenggao, and encamped at Guangwu, drawing provisions from Aocang.
translations.idiomatic: King Han led troops across the river, recaptured Chenggao, and encamped at Guangwu, drawing provisions from Aocang.

sentences.zh: 羽下梁地十餘城，聞海春侯破，乃引兵還。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu took over 10 cities in Liang territory. He heard that Hai Chun Marquis was defeated, so he led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu took over 10 cities in Liang territory. He heard that Hai Chun Marquis was defeated, so he led troops back.

sentences.zh: 漢軍方圍鍾離辚於滎陽東，聞羽至，盡走險阻。

translations.literal: The Han army was surrounding Zhongli Mo east of Xingyang. When they heard Xiang Yu had arrived, they all fled to difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The Han army was surrounding Zhongli Mo east of Xingyang. When they heard Xiang Yu had arrived, they all fled to difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 羽亦軍廣武，與漢相守。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu also encamped at Guangwu and confronted Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu also encamped at Guangwu and confronted Han.

sentences.zh: 丁壯苦軍旅，老弱罷轉餉。

translations.literal: The able-bodied suffered from military campaigns, the old and weak were exhausted from transporting provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The able-bodied suffered from military campaigns, the old and weak were exhausted from transporting provisions.

sentences.zh: 漢王、羽相與臨廣武之間而語。

translations.literal: King Han and Xiang Yu faced each other across Guangwu and spoke.
translations.idiomatic: King Han and Xiang Yu faced each other across Guangwu and spoke.

sentences.zh: 羽欲與漢王獨身挑戰，漢王數羽曰：「吾始與羽俱受命懷王，曰先定關中者王之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge King Han to single combat. King Han listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "I and Xiang Yu both received commands from King Huai, saying whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge the King of Han to single combat. The King of Han instead listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "At first, Xiang Yu and I both received King Huai's command, which said that whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king there.

sentences.zh: 羽負約，王我於蜀漢，罪一也。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu broke the agreement and enfeoffed me as king in Shu and Han. This is crime one.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu broke the agreement and enfeoffed me as king in Shu and Han. This is crime one.

sentences.zh: 羽矯殺卿子冠軍，自尊，罪二也。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu falsely killed Champion Marquis Qing Bu and exalted himself. This is crime two.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu forged orders and killed Lord Champion of the Lords Song Yi, then exalted himself. This is crime two.

sentences.zh: 羽當以救趙還報，而擅劫諸侯兵入關，罪三也。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu should have returned after rescuing Zhao, but instead usurped the feudal lords' troops to enter the passes. This is crime three.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu should have returned after rescuing Zhao, but instead usurped the feudal lords' troops to enter the passes. This is crime three.

sentences.zh: 懷王約入秦無暴掠，羽燒秦宮室，掘始皇帝冢，收私其財，罪四也。

translations.literal: King Huai agreed that entering Qin should not involve violence or plunder, but Xiang Yu burned the Qin palaces, dug up the First Emperor's tomb, and took the treasures for himself. This is crime four.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai's agreement was that whoever entered Qin should commit no violence or plunder, yet Xiang Yu burned the Qin palaces, dug up the First Emperor's tomb, and took the wealth for himself. This is the fourth crime.

sentences.zh: 又彊殺秦降王子嬰，罪五也。

translations.literal: He also forcibly killed the Qin surrender prince Zi Ying. This is crime five.
translations.idiomatic: He also forcibly killed the Qin surrender prince Zi Ying. This is crime five.

sentences.zh: 詐阬秦子弟新安二十萬，王其將，罪六也。

translations.literal: He deceitfully massacred 200,000 Qin youths at Xin'an and made himself their king. This is crime six.
translations.idiomatic: He deceitfully massacred 200,000 Qin soldiers at Xin'an and enfeoffed their generals. This is crime six.

sentences.zh: 皆王諸將善地，而徙逐故主，令臣下爭畔逆，罪七也。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the various generals with good territories but banished and drove out the former lords, causing ministers and subordinates to contend in rebellion. This is crime seven.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed the various generals with good territories, but displaced and drove out the former lords, causing their ministers and subjects to compete in rebellion. This is the seventh crime.

sentences.zh: 出逐義帝彭城，自都之，奪韓王地，并王梁楚，多自與，罪八也。

translations.literal: He drove out Righteous Emperor from Pengcheng, established his own capital there, seized the lands of the King of Han, and united the kingships of Liang and Chu, taking most for himself. This is crime eight.
translations.idiomatic: He drove out the Righteous Emperor to Pengcheng, made it his own capital, seized King Cheng of Han's territory, merged the domains of Liang and Chu under himself, and kept most of the gain for himself. This is crime eight.

sentences.zh: 使人陰殺義帝江南，罪九也。

translations.literal: He sent people to secretly kill Righteous Emperor south of the Jiang. This is crime nine.
translations.idiomatic: He sent people to secretly kill Righteous Emperor south of the Jiang. This is crime nine.

sentences.zh: 夫為人臣而殺其主，殺其已降，為政不平，主約不信，天下所不容，大逆無道，罪十也。

translations.literal: To be a minister and kill one's lord, kill those who have already surrendered, administer government unfairly, break covenants without faith - the world cannot tolerate this. Great rebellion without righteousness. This is crime ten.
translations.idiomatic: To be a minister and kill one's lord, to kill men who have already surrendered, to govern without fairness, and to preside over agreements without good faith - these are things the world cannot tolerate. This is great rebellion and the absence of the Way. This is the tenth crime.

sentences.zh: 吾以義兵從諸侯誅殘賊，使刑餘罪人擊公，何苦乃與公挑戰！」

translations.literal: I lead righteous troops following the feudal lords to execute the cruel and treacherous, using criminals to strike at you. Why must I challenge you to single combat!"
translations.idiomatic: I lead righteous troops with the feudal lords to punish this tyrant. I will send a mutilated convict to fight you—why should I bother dueling you myself!"

sentences.zh: 羽大怒，伏弩射中漢王。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王傷胸，乃捫足曰：「虜中吾指！」

translations.literal: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"
translations.idiomatic: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"

sentences.zh: 漢王病創臥，張良彊請漢王起行勞軍，以安士卒，毋令楚乘勝。

translations.literal: King Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged King Han to rise and go encourage the troops to stabilize the soldiers and officers, not letting Chu take advantage of their victory.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged him to get up and go comfort the army, in order to steady the officers and soldiers and not let Chu exploit its victory.

sentences.zh: 漢王出行軍，疾甚，因馳入成皋。

translations.literal: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 十一月，韓信與灌嬰擊破楚軍，殺楚將龍且，追至城陽，虜齊王廣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Han Xin and Guan Ying attacked and broke the Chu army, killed Chu general Long Ju, pursued to Chengyang, and captured King Qi Tian Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Han Xin and Guan Ying attacked and defeated the Chu army, killed the Chu general Long Ju, pursued as far as Chengyang, and captured Tian Guang, King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊相田橫自立為齊王，奔彭越。

translations.literal: Qi chancellor Tian Heng established himself as King of Qi and fled to Peng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Qi chancellor Tian Heng established himself as King of Qi and fled to Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 漢立張耳為趙王。

translations.literal: Han established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 漢王疾瘉，西入關，至櫟陽，存問父老，置酒。

translations.literal: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.

sentences.zh: 梟故塞王欣頭櫟陽市。

translations.literal: He displayed the head of the former King Sai Xin in Queyang marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed the head of the former King Sai Xin in Queyang marketplace.

sentences.zh: 留四日，復如軍，軍廣武。

translations.literal: He stayed four days, then returned to the army, encamping at Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed four days, then returned to the army, encamping at Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 關中兵益出，而彭越、田橫居梁地，往來苦楚兵，絕其糧食。

translations.literal: Guanzhong troops came out in greater numbers, while Peng Yue and Tian Heng occupied Liang territory, going back and forth to harass Chu troops and cut off their grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: More troops came out from Guanzhong, while Peng Yue and Tian Heng held Liang territory, moving back and forth to harass the Chu troops and cut off their food supply.

sentences.zh: 韓信已破齊，使人言曰：「齊邊楚，權輕，不為假王，恐不能安齊。」

translations.literal: Han Xin had already broken Qi and sent someone to say: "Qi borders Chu. My authority is light. If not made a puppet king, I fear I cannot pacify Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin had already defeated Qi and sent someone to say: "Qi borders Chu and my authority is slight. If I am not made acting king, I fear I cannot pacify Qi."

sentences.zh: 漢王怒，欲攻之。

translations.literal: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.

sentences.zh: 張良曰：「不如因而立之，使自為守。」

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said: "It would be better to take advantage of this and establish him as king, letting him defend it himself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said: "It would be better to take advantage of this and establish him as king, letting him defend it himself."

sentences.zh: 春二月，遣張良操印，立韓信為齊王。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring, he sent Zhang Liang carrying the seal to establish Han Xin as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, he sent Zhang Liang carrying the seal to establish Han Xin as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，立黥布為淮南王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, he established Ying Bu as King of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, he established Ying Bu as King of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 八月，初為算賦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he first established poll taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, he first established poll taxes.

sentences.zh: 北貉、燕人來致梟騎助漢。

translations.literal: The Beidi and Yan people came to deliver owl-headed cavalry to assist Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Beidi and Yan people came to deliver owl-headed cavalry to assist Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王下令：軍士不幸死者，吏為衣衾棺斂，轉送其家。

translations.literal: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.
translations.idiomatic: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.

sentences.zh: 四方歸心焉。

translations.literal: The four directions turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: The four directions turned their hearts to him.

sentences.zh: 項羽自知少助食盡，韓信又進兵擊楚，羽患之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu knew he had few helpers and food was exhausted. Han Xin again advanced troops to attack Chu. Xiang Yu was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu knew that he had few allies and that his food was exhausted. Han Xin was again advancing troops to attack Chu, and Xiang Yu was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 漢遣陸賈說羽，請太公，羽弗聽。

translations.literal: Han sent Lu Jia to persuade Xiang Yu to return the Duke of Tai. Xiang Yu did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Lu Jia to persuade Xiang Yu to return the Duke of Tai. Xiang Yu did not listen.

sentences.zh: 漢復使侯公說羽，羽乃與漢約，中分天下，割鴻溝以西為漢，以東為楚。

translations.literal: Han again sent Hou Gong to persuade Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu then made a treaty with Han to divide the world in half, giving Honggou west to Han and east to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Han again sent Hou Gong to persuade Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu then made an agreement with Han to divide the realm in two, assigning the lands west of Honggou to Han and those east of it to Chu.

sentences.zh: 九月，歸太公、呂后，軍皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 乃封侯公為平國君。

translations.literal: He then enfeoffed Hou Gong as Lord of Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He then enfeoffed Hou Gong as Lord of Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 羽解而東歸。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu withdrew and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu withdrew and returned east.

sentences.zh: 漢王欲西歸，張良、陳平諫曰：「今漢有天下太半，而諸侯皆附，楚兵罷食盡，此天亡之時，不因其幾而遂取之，所謂養虎自遺患也。」

translations.literal: King Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised: "Now Han possesses more than half the world, and all the feudal lords are attached. Chu troops are exhausted and food is finished. This is the time Heaven has doomed them. If we do not take advantage of this opportunity to destroy them, this is called raising a tiger that brings disaster to oneself."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised him: "Han now possesses more than half the realm, and all the feudal lords have attached themselves to it. Chu's troops are exhausted and its food is gone. This is the moment when Heaven is destroying Chu. If we do not seize this opportunity and take it, that is what is called raising a tiger and leaving disaster for oneself."

sentences.zh: 漢王從之。

translations.literal: King Han followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: King Han followed their advice.
